Position: Management Trainee – Supply Chain Management

The Management Trainee – SCM will support Bigmart’s supply chain operations by driving warehouse efficiency, cost optimization, and process improvement initiatives. The role involves analyzing operational data, evaluating workflows, conducting DC visits, and piloting scalable solutions. It also focuses on inventory accuracy, stock movement, and cross-functional collaboration to strengthen warehouse operations and operational excellence.

Location: Bigmart Head Office & DCs/Warehouses within and outside Kathmandu Valley
No of Vacancy: 1
Work Schedule: 10 AM-6 PM (Training-period flexibility required, including overnight and early-morning shifts)

ONE YEAR TRAINING PERIOD:

One-year training across Bigmart’s DCs/ warehouses within and outside Kathmandu Valley, with flexible locations and rotational shifts including:

9:00 PM – 5:00 AM
3:00 AM – 11:00 AM
4:00 AM – 12:00 PM
7:00 AM – 3:00 PM
10:00 AM – 6:00 PM

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES AFTER TRAINING:

  • Lead lean-cost initiatives and pilots to reduce waste and costs without affecting service levels.
  • Review workflows to identify inefficiencies and improve efficiency and cost-effectiveness.
  • Conduct regular DC visits to identify bottlenecks and align strategy with site execution.
  • Report project progress, cost savings, and KPIs to the Sr. SCM Manager.
  • Drive planning and analytics for inventory, dispatch, stock accuracy, and OOS analysis.
  • Pilot process improvements and recommend successful initiatives for wider rollout.
  • Monitor stock movement, inventory accuracy, and adherence to warehouse best practices.
  • Coordinate with internal teams and external stakeholders for smooth implementation.
  • Mentor warehouse teams to sustain improved processes.

JOB SPECIFICATIONS:

  • Education and Qualifications: Master’s degree in Management (MBA, MBS, or MBM or related field), preferably with Finance specialization, and strong academic performance in Mathematics and related subjects at Bachelor’s and Master’s levels.
  • Experiences: 1-2 years of relevant FMCG experience in logistics, inventory, procurement, or warehousing preferred.

Skills and Competencies:

  • Experience in warehouse/supply chain cost optimization or lean operations.
  • Strong data analysis and actionable insight skills.
  • Willingness to travel frequently to Distribution Centers (within and outside Kathmandu Valley).
  • Strong project management and process-scaling skills.
  • Ability to work independently with structured reporting.
  • Knowledge of ERP/WMS, inventory systems, KPIs, and compliance.
  • Strong stakeholder management and cross-functional collaboration.
  • Adaptability to a fast-growing business environment.
  • Must have valid 2-wheeler driving license and own vehicle.
  • Willingness to travel and work overnight and early-morning shifts during training phase.

Apply now and be a part of Bigmart’s SCM Department

Interested and eligible candidates may send their updated CV and Bachelors transcript and Masters transcript (Mandatory) to vacancy@bigmart.com.np with “SCM Management Trainee” clearly mentioned in the subject line.

Deadline to Apply: September 16, 2026 (Bhadra 31, 2083)

Note: Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted

Job Title: Project Officer-Financial Inclusion
Position Number: TBD
New or Refill: New
Core position: Yes/ No
Salary Grade: 3
Division/Dept.: Programs/Asia
Dept. #/Subproject WO: TBD/ Signature Program-LAGANI
Reports to: Project Manager- PROSPER
Supervisor POSNO: TBD
Supervisor RESNO/Name: TBD
Supervision: Employees Yes No | Volunteers Yes No
Location: Project Area of PROSPER (Surkhet, Bardiya, Bake and Dang)
Relocation Funds: Not allotted
Travel Required: Minimum 70% Annually

Heifer Project Nepal is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, religion, color, national origin, gender, gender identify, sexual orientation, age, status as a protected veteran, among other things, or status as a qualified individual with disability.

FUNCTION

The Financial Inclusion Officer-Financial Inclusion will lead the PROSPER project’s financial inclusion portfolio, providing strategic and technical support to improve farmers’, cooperatives’, and SMEs’ access to appropriate finance, markets, and enterprise-development opportunities.

The role will strengthen stakeholder capacity, facilitate partnerships with financial institutions, fintech/agritech firms, buyers, and investors, support farmer-friendly financing initiatives such as FEBL Lite, oversee loan facilitation and repayment performance, and provide timely analysis and recommendations to the Project Manager and thematic leads.

Financial Inclusion and Technical Assistance (50%)

  • Lead financial, business, and digital literacy initiatives, including FEBL Lite, through Bank Saathis, digital facilitators, and tools such as GeoKrishi Farm.
  • Strengthen cooperatives as inclusive business and financial-service hubs by improving governance, financial management, digital systems, and service delivery.
  • Establish and manage Bank Saathi networks to support farmers with loan applications, credit histories, insurance, repayment planning, and digital financial services.
  • Collaborate with BFIs, fintech firms, and other partners to design, pilot, and scale inclusive credit, insurance, and green-finance products for smallholder farmers, women, youth, persons with disabilities, returnee migrants, and agribusinesses.
  • Support loan documentation, responsible use of finance, repayment monitoring, and the adoption of digital tools that improve transparency and reduce transaction costs.
  • Facilitate enterprise development and market linkages through buyer mapping, business-to-business engagement, aggregation, fair contracts, and investment opportunities.
  • Engage local governments and regulators to promote an inclusive, gender-responsive, and climate-sensitive financial ecosystem.
  • Develop and implement structured training, coaching, and mentoring plans for project staff, partners, cooperatives, Bank Saathis, agribusinesses, and farmers.
  • Strengthen business planning, financial management, marketing, negotiation, investment readiness, and market-linkage capacities.
  • Mentor Bank Saathis and cooperatives to improve financial-service outreach, farmer support, and cooperative–bank relationships.
  • Support cooperatives and enterprises to access productive infrastructure, equipment, finance, and cost-sharing opportunities.
  • Develop practical training materials and tools on financial literacy, enterprise development, value chains, and market access.

Collaboration, Partnership and Resource Leveraging (30%)

  • Coordinate with local governments, Heifer teams, BFIs, MFIs, insurance companies, agri-tech/fintech firms, private sector actors, buyers, investors, and value chain stakeholders.
  • Develop inclusive partnership models such as cooperative-bank partnerships, contract farming, out-grower schemes, joint ventures, buyback guarantees, MoUs, and risk-sharing arrangements.
  • Facilitate exposure visits, networking events, trade fairs, and co-design meetings to promote learning, investment, and inclusive business development.
  • Advocate for farmer-friendly financial systems, simplified documentation, improved trust between farmers and BFIs, and reduced transaction costs.
  • Leverage public, private, and philanthropic resources to support enterprise growth, dairy sector development, and market system strengthening.

Monitoring, Review, Documentation and Reporting (15%)

  • Conduct regular field visits to monitor project progress, financial tool adoption, loan disbursement, utilization, repayment, business growth, and partnership performance.
  • Track income improvement, employment generation, borrower feedback, market deals, bankable business plans, and success stories.
  • Maintain updated records on producers, production, yield, marketable quantities, buyers, cooperatives, financial institution linkages, and training participation.
  • Prepare field visit notes, event reports, monthly progress reports, repayment trend analysis, and recommendations for improvement.
  • Ensure reports include disaggregated participant data, key outcomes, challenges, lessons learned, and follow-up actions for the regional and LAGANI Signature Program through Project Manager.

May perform other job-related duties as assigned (5%)

QUALIFICATIONS AND SKILLS

  • Bachelor’s degree in economics, management, agriculture/agribusiness, or a related field with (5) five years of relevant experience; or a master’s degree with (3) three years of experience.
  • Proven experience in financial inclusion, loan and investment facilitation, field-program monitoring, and engagement with financial institutions and private sector actors.
  • Experience in agricultural value chains, market linkages, investment promotion, and agriculture or livestock enterprise development.
  • Experience supporting smallholder farmers, cooperatives, agri-enterprises, or agrifood processors, women, person with disability and youth is an advantage.
  • Strong leadership, stakeholder management, coaching, teamwork, analytical, and problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to work independently, take initiative, and manage diverse teams.
  • Fluency in spoken and written Nepali and English.

ESSENTIAL COMPETENCIES AND TRAITS:

  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook) and virtual collaboration tools.
  • Demonstrate the ability to handle confidential and sensitive information with professionalism while promoting transparency, ethical decision making, and accountability in all aspects of work.
  • The ability to work effectively and respectfully with people from diverse cultural, social, and professional backgrounds.
  • Strong organizational and time management skills.
  • Willingness to work flexibly and ability to travel extensively to rural and project locations to strengthen the relationship to support partners and ensure effective implementation.
  • Demonstrated commitment to Heifer International’s mission, values, and regenerative, locally led program approach.
  • Sensitivity in working with multiple cultures and beliefs, and gender equity.

Position Number: TBD

Travel Required: Minimum 70% annually

Heifer Project Nepal (HPN) is an equal-opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, status as a protected veteran, among other things, or status as a qualified individual with some form of especially abled.

FUNCTION:
The Project Manager – PROSPER will lead and coordinate the effective implementation of the PROSPER project.

  • Project Management: Lead project setup, planning, implementation, monitoring, evaluation, review, and feedback processes in line with PMD Pro standards.
  • Partner Management: Coordinate technical and implementing partners, strengthen partner capacity, promote private-sector engagement, and leverage additional resources.
  • People Management: Coach and mentor staff, build team capacity, foster a supportive working environment, solve problems, and make evidence-based decisions to achieve project results.

The Program Manager is responsible for adaptive management of the project in alignment with Heifer International’s regenerative program model. The role works to enables cross-functional collaboration and strategic partnerships with the LAGANI Signature Program team, technical partners, implementing partners, farmer organizations, private sector actors, and governments to deliver high-quality, timely, and budget-compliant project outcomes.

The Project Manager is also responsible to strengthen local systems and institutional capacities, promote inclusive market systems and access to finance, support an enabling policy and regulatory environment, and ensures robust planning, monitoring, learning, accountability, and knowledge sharing to achieve sustainable impact and contribute to the broader objectives of the Signature Program.

RESPONSIBILITIES AND DELIVERABLES: (including approximate percentage effort)

Project management (50 %)

  • Lead project planning, budget management, expenditure tracking, and evidence-based decision-making.
  • Ensure achievement of project KPIs.
  • Manage project staff and partners to ensure approved work plans and activities are implemented efficiently and effectively.
  • Ensure the project is delivered on time, within budget, and within the approved scope.
  • Oversee monitoring, evaluation, and reporting in line with Heifer’s MELS framework, donor requirements, and statutory obligations.
  • Maintain quality assurance, accountability, and compliance throughout the project lifecycle.
  • Lead the selection and engagement of cooperatives, farmer organizations, farmer clusters, and implementation areas, ensuring the inclusion of smallholder farmers, particularly women and youth.
  • Supervise project officers and partner staff responsible for access to finance, training, digital interventions, and field-level implementation.

Partnership and leveraging (25%)

  • Co-develop and periodically update the project implementation plan with the local partners, regional leads and LAGANI team, if needed with the relevant staff of Milky Way and SAFAL programs.
  • Build and manage strategic partnerships with BFIs, insurers, agri-tech and fintech firms, buyers, service providers, government agencies, NGOs, and cooperative associations to connect cooperatives and farmers with finance, markets, technology, and services.
  • Convene stakeholders through local Multi-Stakeholder Platforms to address financial inclusion barriers and promote gender-responsive and climate-intentional solutions for rural women, Person with Disabilities (PWD) and youth.
  • Mobilize and leverage public, private, philanthropic, and development resources, including government co-financing, private-sector investment, and financing from banks and MFIs to scale and sustain project results.

Knowledge management, technical and policy support (20%)

  • Develop and update program manuals, guidelines, procedures, implementation plans, and FEBL Lite training materials in line with Heifer standards, donor requirements, and statutory regulations.
  • Document lessons, innovations, good practices, and results from financial inclusion and policy interventions to support learning, replication, and scale-up.
  • Provide technical assistance and capacity-building to project staff, partners, cooperatives, farmers, and SMEs to strengthen financial literacy, access to finance, and effective follow-up.
  • Promote cooperative-led and technology-enabled financial systems, including relevant agri-tech and fintech solutions, to improve access to formal finance.
  • Identify financial inclusion barriers and facilitate evidence-based dialogue through local Multi-Stakeholder Platforms.
  • Translate field evidence into practical policy recommendations and support government and other stakeholders in creating an enabling environment for inclusive finance, with a focus on smallholder farmers, women, youth, and rural SMEs.

May perform other job-related duties as assigned (5%)

QUALIFICATIONS AND SKILLS:

  • A bachelor’s degree in business administration, economics, agriculture or a related field with a minimum of five (5) years of managerial experience, or a master’s degree in any of the above fields with at least three (3) years of relevant managerial experience.
  • Demonstrated experience in financial inclusion, digital finance, community mobilization, social capital development, institutional development, capacity building, training, smallholder farmers/rural SMEs/co-ops, and base of the pyramid consumers.
  • Previous experience in facilitation of investment in agri-enterprises, cooperatives or smallholder farmers, agrifood processing will be considered an added advantage.
  • Strong collaboration and relationship management skills.
  • Ability to lead, coach and mentor diverse teams to foster an inclusive and collaborative work environment.
  • Ability to work independently and take initiative while also having strong team-building skills
  • Strong analytical, problem solving, and decision-making skills.
  • Fluent in Nepali and English languages (both spoken and written).
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook) and virtual collaboration tools.
  • Excellent leadership qualities.

ESSENTIAL COMPETENCIES:

  • Demonstrate the ability to handle confidential and sensitive information with professionalism while promoting transparency, ethical decision making, and accountability in all aspects of work.
  • The ability to work effectively and respectfully with people from diverse cultural, social, and professional backgrounds.
  • Strong organizational and time management skills.
  • Willingness to work flexibly and ability to travel extensively to rural and project locations to strengthen the relationship to support partners and ensure effective implementation.
  • Demonstrated commitment to Heifer International’s mission, values, and regenerative, locally led program approach.
  • Sensitivity in working with multiple cultures and beliefs, and gender equity.

The Project Coordinator will play a key role in promoting disability-inclusive humanitarian response and recovery by ensuring that planned project activities are implemented on time, within budget, and to a high standard, in close coordination with consortium and implementing partners.

The position will lead and coordinate consortium teams NDWA and BYAN, oversee project implementation and partnerships, monitor the use of resources and achievement of results, ensure compliance and accountability and coordinate with government authorities, humanitarian actors, development partners, and other relevant stakeholders.

NFDN is seeking a qualified, experienced and motivated Finance Officer to support the financial management of its program operation at various projects. The Finance Officer will be responsible for ensuring sound financial management, accounting, budgeting, financial reporting, compliance, and documentation of the project expenditure in accordance with NFDN policies, donor requirements, applicable laws, and agreements with partners. The position will work closely with the project team, consortium/implementing partners, NFDN Finance and Administration team, and relevant stakeholders to ensure effective and transparent utilization of project resources.

The Finance Officer will be based at NFDN Federal Office, Kathmandu, and will report to the Chief Finance Officer and Admin Manager.

Financial Management and Accounting

  • Ensure proper and timely recording of all project financial transactions in accordance with NFDN’s Financial Management and Accounting policies and procedures.

  • Support preparation of project budgets, budget revisions, cash forecasts, and financial plans.
  • Monitor project expenditure against approved budgets and provide regular budget-versus-actual analysis.

  • Support project teams in understanding budget requirements and ensuring efficient utilization of resources.
  • Monitor financial performance of implementing and consortium partners in accordance with partnership agreements.

Financial Reporting and Compliance

  • Prepare timely and accurate monthly, quarterly, donor, and project financial reports as required.
  • Support preparation of financial reports and statements for donors and partners in accordance with their requirements.
  • Ensure compliance with NFDN financial policies, donor rules, project agreements, and applicable Government of Nepal regulations.
  • Ensure that financial documentation is complete, properly filed, and readily available for internal and external audits.

Internal Control and Risk Management

  • Ensure effective internal financial controls are maintained throughout project implementation.
  • Identify financial risks and recommend appropriate mitigation measures.
  • Monitor compliance with procurement and financial procedures.
  • Support prevention and detection of financial irregularities, fraud, misuse of resources, and conflicts of interest.
  • Ensure appropriate segregation of financial responsibilities and authorization controls.

Other Responsibilities

  • Support emergency response teams with rapid financial arrangements when required.
  • Provide financial inputs for project proposals, budgets, concept notes, and reports.
  • Maintain confidentiality and integrity of financial information.
  • Contribute to organizational learning and improvement of financial systems.

Eligibility to Apply

Education: At least Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Management, Commerce, or a related field.

Experience

  • Experience in budget preparation, expenditure monitoring, financial analysis, and financial reporting.

Skills and Competencies

  • Ability to review financial documents carefully and identify errors, inconsistencies, and compliance issues.
  • Ability to work independently and manage multiple priorities under pressure.
  • Strong coordination and communication skills.

Blind Youth Association Nepal (BYAN) is seeking a qualified, motivated, and committed Youth Engagement Officer (Emergency Response) to support the implementation of a disability inclusive emergency response initiative in Nuwakot, Rasuwa, and Dhading, Nepal.

The project will be implemented from September 2026 to February 2027 in collaboration with the National Federation of the Disabled Nepal (NFDN) and Nepal Disabled Women Association (NDWA), with support from CBM Global Disability Inclusion Nepal.

As a sub-partner, BYAN will contribute to strengthening the meaningful engagement and participation of young persons with disabilities in emergency response, with particular attention to girls and young persons with disabilities. The project will promote access to sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR), empowerment, information, protection, and essential services, while strengthening the capacity of frontline responders and promoting disability-inclusive emergency response practices.

Position: Youth Engagement Officer (Emergency Response)

Duty Station: Nuwakot, Nepal, with regular travel to project locations in Rasuwa and Dhading and other areas as required.

Key Responsibilities

  • Coordinate and support the implementation of BYAN’s activities under the disability-inclusive emergency response initiative in close coordination with NFDN, NDWA, CBM Global, local governments, and other relevant stakeholders.
  • Promote meaningful participation and leadership of youth with disabilities in emergency response planning, implementation, monitoring, and advocacy.
  • Engage with girls and young persons with disabilities, including those at heightened risk, and facilitate access to sRHR information and services, empowerment opportunities, protection mechanisms, and other available services and benefits.
  • Support identification of barriers faced by persons with disabilities in accessing emergency services and facilitate appropriate referrals and linkages with service providers.
  • Conduct or support disability inclusion orientations and awareness sessions for frontline responders, including FCHVs, health service providers, security personnel, local authorities, and other relevant actors.
  • Support walk-through accessibility audits of holding centres, temporary shelters, temporary learning centres, health facilities, and other emergency response sites, and document accessibility gaps and recommendations.
  • Support disability-inclusive communication and information dissemination, ensuring that emergency information and key service messages are accessible to persons with different disabilities.
  • Design and implement social media and digital awareness campaigns on disability-inclusive emergency response, youth participation, sRHR, protection, accessibility, and access to services.
  • Mobilize and engage youth volunteers, youth networks, disability organizations, and other community actors in emergency response-related activities.
  • Support the collection of disability-disaggregated information and community feedback to identify emerging needs, barriers, risks, and gaps in emergency response services.
  • Document good practices, challenges, case stories, lessons learned, and emerging evidence related to disability-inclusive emergency response and youth engagement.
  • Maintain regular communication and coordination with BYAN, NFDN, NDWA, CBM Global, other project partners, local government representatives, frontline responders, and other relevant stakeholders.
  • Ensure that activities are implemented in accordance with approved project plans, safeguarding and PSEAH standards, and relevant organizational policies and procedures.
  • Support monitoring, reporting, documentation, accountability to affected populations, and learning related to project interventions.
  • Undertake other duties relevant to the position as assigned by BYAN management.

Required Qualifications and Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree in Social Sciences, Development Studies, Public Health, Social Work, Disability Studies, or a related field. A Master’s degree will be an advantage.
  • At least 2 years of relevant professional experience in disability inclusion, youth engagement, humanitarian/emergency response, community mobilization, sRHR, protection, or related areas.
  • Demonstrated understanding of disability rights, disability inclusion, and meaningful participation of persons with disabilities.

Duties

The position is located in the Library of Congress office, US Embassy Nepal and functions as the designated liaison for the Library of Congress in Nepal. Incumbent is supervised by the Field Director for South Asia posted in US Embassy New Delhi, India.

The incumbent acquires and creates online bibliographic records for publications in all languages and formats published in Nepal for the collections of the Library of Congress in Washington D.C., and for libraries of American and Canadian universities who participate in the South Asia Cooperative Acquisitions Program (SACAP). Reviews and critically selects publications in all various formats. Evaluates each publication to determine its research, literary or documentary value, degree of contribution to the body of published literature, originality and conformance to the collection policies of the Library of Congress and SACAP participants. Keeps abreast of publishing trends in Nepal by regularly accessing online and print resources such as scholarly publications, newspapers, catalogs, etc. Ensures identification, recommendations, and acquisitions of “in-scope” electronic and print publications which reflect current sociopolitical, economic, cultural, religious, and legal environments in Nepal.

Posiiton: Emergency Finance Officer
Location: Kathmandu with frequent travel to project working areas
Position Status: Full-time, Contract

About Mercy Corps

Mercy Corps is a leading global organization powered by the belief that a better world is possible. In disaster, in hardship, in more than 40 countries around the world, we partner to put bold solutions into action — helping people triumph over adversity and build stronger communities from within. Now, and for the future.

The Program Summary

On 26 August 2026, a glacier and rockfall avalanche near the Rasuwagadhi border triggered a catastrophic debris-flow flood along the Bhotekoshi–Trishuli corridor, severely affecting Rasuwa, Nuwakot, and Dhading, districts. Search and rescue operations led by NDRRMA and other responders are ongoing. The disaster has resulted in significant loss of life, injuries, displacement, and extensive damage to infrastructure and livelihoods. Thousands of affected people are facing critical shortages of shelter, water, food, and sanitation supplies. Mercy Corps Nepal is responding to the disaster supporting the affected families with immediate relief and enabling recovery.

The Position (General Position Summary)

The Emergency Finance Officer is responsible for supporting day to day financial operations of the emergency response project ensuring accuracy, timeliness and compliance with Mercy Corps Nepal policiesand regulatory requirements. This position is responsible for processing payments, managing bank-related activities, maintaining accurate accounting records in the financial system, and supporting month-end reconciliations and work closely with partner organization ensuring financial management of partner organization.

Essential Job Responsibilities
The specific duties and responsibilities of the Emergency Finance Officer include, but are not limited to, the following:

FINANCE MANAGEMENT

  • Manage day to day financial operations of the project ensuring compliance with Mercy Corps Nepal policies and other regulatory requirements.
  • Prepare cash flows, monitor project expenditures, and ensure sufficient liquidity for field operations.
  • Process payments, advances and settlements and maintain accurate accounting records and supporting documentation.
  • Manage bank-related correspondence including signatory updates and other communication.
  • Conduct day-to-day data entries into Accounting Software Navigator, ensuring data accuracy and compliance with applicable policies and guidelines.
  • File all vouchers and supporting documents and support proper maintenance of project-related files archive.
  • Review partner/sub-recipient Fund Transfer requests and reconcile with partner financial reports and Navigator data.
  • Prepare photocopies, scans, and other required supporting documents for monthly reporting packages to HQ Finance.
  • Ensure financial management of partner organization and support on financial management capacity building.

COMPLIANCE AND RISK MANAGEMENT

  • Ensure compliance with donor requirements and organizational policies.
  • Support internal and external audits.

COORDINATION AND REPORTING

  • Conduct regular budget monitoring and provides budget Vs expenses analysis to the emergency response coordinator.
  • Support the Interim Senior Finance and Compliance Coordinator in preparation of financial reports, forecasts, and donor financial documentation.
  • Participate in project planning, coordination meetings and emergency response activities as required.
  • Prepare monthly Cash and Bank Reconciliations and get them approved and filed as required.

SAFEGUARDING RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Actively learns about safeguarding and integrates it into their work, including safeguarding risks and mitigations related to their area of work.
  • Practices the values of Mercy Corps including respecting the dignity and well-being of participants and fellow team members.
  • Encourages openness and communication in their team; encourages team members to submit reports if they have any concerns using reporting mechanisms e.g., Integrity Hotline and other options.

Supervisory Responsibility: N/A

Accountability

Reports Directly To: Interim Senior Finance and Compliance Coordinator

Works Directly With: Emergency Response Coordinator and project technical partner team members as required.

Accountability to Participants and Stakeholders

Mercy Corps team members are expected to support all efforts toward accountability, specifically to our program participants, community partners, other stakeholders, and to international standards guiding international relief and development work. We are committed to actively engaging communities as equal partners in the design, monitoring and evaluation of our field projects.

Minimum Qualification & Transferable Skills

  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent in accounting/ financial management or a relevant business field.
  • Minimum of 3-5 years of relevant experience in finance and accounting. Working experience with I/NGOs is preferred.
  • Knowledge of GoN tax regulations, VAT, and TDS requirements.
  • Demonstrated attention to detail, ability to follow procedures, meet deadlines, and work independently and cooperatively with team members.
  • Proficiency in MS Office programs, particularly Excel and financial/accounting software.
  • Excellent coordination and communication skills.
  • Strong planning, organizational, and reporting skills.
  • Ability to work effectively with an ethnically diverse team in a sensitive environment.
  • Experience in emergency response or disaster management is preferred.

Success Factors

A successful Finance officer should have a clear understanding of finance and procurement ethics as well as the willingness and ability to enforce compliance with Mercy Corps and donor policies and procedures is essential. A demonstrated ability to work quickly and accurately, meet deadlines, and process information in support of changing program activities is necessary. Multi-tasking, prioritizing, problem-solving and simultaneous attention to detail are essential.

S/he will have proven ability to learn quickly, take initiative, and be accountable for results, with an ability and willingness to remain mobile for short-term and/or long-term as necessary within the region, based on programmatic needs. An ability to work independently and as part of a team, with curiosity about and sensitivity to new cultures, a desire and ability to learn and grow, both personally and professionally, and a great sense of humor.

The most successful Mercy Corps team members have a strong commitment to teamwork and accountability, thrive in evolving and changing environments and make effective written and verbal communication a priority in all situations.

Living Conditions / Environmental Conditions

The position is based in Kathmandu, Nepal and it requires up to 40% travel to support country programs, which may include travel to insecure locations where freedom of movement is limited and areas where amenities are limited.

Ongoing Learning

In support of our belief that learning organizations are more effective, efficient and relevant to the communities we serve, we empower all team members to dedicate 5% of their time to learning activities that further their personal and/or professional growth and development.

Team Engagement and Effectiveness

Achieving our mission starts with how we build our team and collaborate. By bringing together individuals with a variety of experiences, backgrounds, and perspectives, we strengthen our ability to solve complex challenges and drive innovation. We foster a culture of trust and respect, where every team member is valued for their contributions, empowered to reach their full potential, and motivated to do their best work.

We recognize that building a strong and effective team is an ongoing process, and we remain committed to learning, improving, and growing together.

Equal Employment Opportunity

Position: Emergency Monitoring Evaluation & Learning (MEL) and Communications Officer
Location: Nuwakot, Nepal
Position Status: Full-time, Contract

About Mercy Corps

Mercy Corps is a leading global organization powered by the belief that a better world is possible. In disaster, in hardship, in more than 40 countries around the world, we partner to put bold solutions into action helping people triumph over adversity and build stronger communities from within. Now, and for the future.

The Program Summary

On 26 August 2026, a glacier and rockfall avalanche near the Rasuwagadhi border triggered a catastrophic debris-flow flood along the Bhotekoshi–Trishuli corridor, severely affecting Rasuwa, Nuwakot, and Dhading, districts. Search and rescue operations led by NDRRMA and other responders are ongoing. The disaster has resulted in significant loss of life, injuries, displacement, and extensive damage to infrastructure and livelihoods. Thousands of affected people are facing critical shortages of shelter, water, food, and sanitation supplies. Mercy Corps Nepal is responding to the disaster supporting the affected families with immediate relief and enabling recovery.

The Position (General Position Summary)

The MEL and Communication Officer support Mercy Corps Nepal’s Emergency Response Program by ensuring monitoring, evaluation and learning systems meet organizational standards, and that program results, learning and best practices are effectively documented and communicated to internal and external stakeholders. The role works closely with the Emergency Response Coordinator, Country MEL Focal Person, and partner to strengthen data quality, participant tracking, and reporting compliance, while also leading communication and knowledge management functions from donor- and media-facing materials to internal learning platforms in line with Mercy Corps’ branding and quality standards.

Essential Job Responsibilities

The specific duties and responsibilities of the MEL and Communications Officer include, but are not limited to, the following:

ASSESSMENT AND MONITORING

  • Support/lead Rapid Needs Assessments (RNA) and contribute to Multi-Sectoral Needs Assessments (MSNA) to inform targeting and response design.
  • Conduct real-time monitoring of response activities against targets, flagging targeting errors, pipeline breaks, or access gaps for immediate correction.
  • Design and conduct Post-Distribution Monitoring (PDM) for cash and in-kind assistance, verifying timeliness, amounts received, use, and continued relevance of transfer values against market prices.
  • Develop compressed, workable MEL frameworks appropriate to the response timeline, and facilitate After Action Reviews (AARs) to document lessons for subsequent response phases.
  • Ensure Mercy Corps’ MEL minimum standards are rolled out and followed across the project/program.
  • Build project team capacity on MEL systems, tools and standards.
  • Plan and facilitate learning events and support thematic teams in capturing and synthesizing field-level learning.

DATA COLLECTION AND QUALITY

  • Design and deploy lean, digital-where-feasible data collection tools appropriate to the acute response phase.
  • Conduct data quality checks and spot verification to ensure reported figures are accurate and defensible.
  • Apply data protection protocols appropriate to the heightened vulnerability of affected populations, including consent and secure storage of PII.

ACCOUNTABILITY

  • Work closely with Country CARM focal person to establish and manage Community Accountability and Response Mechanism (CARM), ensuring safeguarding and protection concerns are identified and referred immediately.
  • Ensure community feedback reaches decisionmakers and informs response adjustments in real time.

COORDINATION AND REPORTING

  • Contribute to 4W/5W coordination reporting to relevant clusters and government entities to avoid duplication and coverage gaps.
  • Track output indicators against cluster standards and produce timely situation reports and donor updates in required formats and timeline.
  • Support Emergency Response Coordinator to prepare periodic progress updates, reports and stories, in collaboration project team, ensuring government and donor compliance.
  • Review project guidelines, documents and resource materials, and prepare shareable resources aligned with Mercy Corps’ and donors’ branding guidelines.

COMMUNICATION AND KNOWLEDGE MANAGEMENT

  • Develop and implement a communication plan to document and disseminate program processes and results to stakeholders.
  • Prepare clear, concise, and compelling reports, presentations and communication materials, and manage internal and external communication channels.
  • Identify and engage key audiences donors, participants and partners through targeted communication strategies and build media relationships to secure positive coverage.
  • Serve as a technical lead for communication and knowledge management, designing and implementing effective tools and mechanisms with the wider team.
  • Capture and document program learning and best practices and organize best-practice-sharing workshops and knowledge products for internal and external audiences.
  • Ensure all communications, outreach and visibility materials comply with the Mercy Corps Nepal Branding Guideline.
  • Collect, structure and maintain project information including a standard information package for internal, external, government and media audiences, ensuring materials remain current and accessible.

SAFEGUARDING RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Actively learns about safeguarding and integrates it into their work, including safeguarding risks and mitigations related to their area of work.
  • Practices the values of Mercy Corps including respecting the dignity and well-being of participants and fellow team members.
  • Encourages openness and communication in their team; encourages team members to submit reports if they have any concerns using reporting mechanisms e.g., Integrity Hotline and other options.

Supervisory Responsibility : N/A

Accountability

Reports Directly To: Emergency Response Coordinator
Works Directly With: Country MEL focal person, CARM Focal person, and partner’s team members.
Accountability to Participants and Stakeholders

Mercy Corps team members are expected to support all efforts toward accountability, specifically to our program participants, community partners, other stakeholders, and to international standards guiding international relief and development work. We are committed to actively engaging communities as equal partners in the design, monitoring and evaluation of our field projects.

Minimum Qualification & Transferable Skills

  • Bachelor’s degree in Development Studies/Management, Mass Communications, or a related discipline; Master’s degree preferred.
  • At least 3–5 years of experience in MEL, communications and/or knowledge management with I/NGOs and/or private sector organizations working in disaster risk management, humanitarian assistance.
    Experience designing and implementing MEL systems, including analyzing and promoting the use of collected data.
  • Demonstrated experience with digital data collection technologies and web-based platforms.
  • Knowledge and practical understanding of accountability, particularly to communities and program participants.
  • Previous experience of building MEL capacity, including developing training tools, training, coaching and mentoring.
  • Communication and knowledge management design and implementation skills.
  • Strong written and oral communication skills in English and Nepali, including report writing, analysis and editing.
  • Strong interpersonal, negotiation and representation skills, demonstrated ability to work effectively across multi-cultural, ethnically diverse teams and stakeholders in sensitive environments.
  • Ability to work in complex environments under tight deadlines and changing donor requirements.
  • Good computer skills, including MS Word, Excel and PowerPoint, and online research/information gathering.
  • Photography and videography skills an added advantage.

Success Factors

A successful candidate will have the ability to live and work closely with a diverse team of individuals in a highly intense and fluid work and security environment with a capacity to spark innovative approaches to programming and inspire groups to collaborate closely to implement high-quality humanitarian programs. S/he will have proven ability to learn quickly, take initiative, and be accountable for results, with an ability and willingness to remain mobile for short-term and/or long-term as necessary within the region, based on programmatic needs. An ability to work independently and as part of a team, with curiosity about and sensitivity to new cultures, a desire and ability to learn and grow, both personally and professionally, and a great sense of humor.

The most successful Mercy Corps team members have a strong commitment to teamwork and accountability, thrive in evolving and changing environments and make effective written and verbal communication a priority in all situations. Mercy Corps Team members represent the agency both during and outside of work hours when deployed in a field posting or on a visit/short-term assignment to a field posting. Team members are expected to conduct themselves in a professional manner and respect local laws, customs and MC’s policies, procedures, and values at all times and in all in-country venues.

Living Conditions / Environmental Conditions

The position is based in Nuwakot, Nepal.

Ongoing Learning

In support of our belief that learning organizations are more effective, efficient and relevant to the communities we serve, we empower all team members to dedicate 5% of their time to learning activities that further their personal and/or professional growth and development.

Team Engagement and Effectiveness

Achieving our mission starts with how we build our team and collaborate. By bringing together individuals with a variety of experiences, backgrounds, and perspectives, we strengthen our ability to solve complex challenges and drive innovation. We foster a culture of trust and respect, where every team member is valued for their contributions, empowered to reach their full potential, and motivated to do their best work.

We recognize that building a strong and effective team is an ongoing process, and we remain committed to learning, improving, and growing together.

Equal Employment Opportunity

Mercy Corps is an equal opportunity employer committed to providing equal employment opportunities to all employees and qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, color, sex, sexual orientation, religion or belief, national origin, age, disability, marital status, veteran status, or any other characteristics protected under applicable law.

Safeguarding & Ethics

Mercy Corps is committed to ensuring that all individuals we come into contact with through our work, whether team members, community members, program participants or others, are treated with respect and dignity. We are committed to the core principles regarding prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse laid out by the UN Secretary General and IASC and have signed on to The Misconduct Disclosure Scheme. We will not tolerate child abuse, sexual exploitation, abuse, or harassment by or of our team members. As part of our commitment to a safe and inclusive work environment, team members are expected to conduct themselves in a professional manner, respect local laws and customs, and to adhere to Mercy Corps Code of Conduct Policies and values at all times. Team members are required to complete mandatory Code of Conduct elearning courses upon hire and on an annual basis.

As an applicant, if you witness or experience any form of sexual misconduct during the recruitment process, please report this to Mercy Corps Integrity Hotline (integrityhotline@mercycorps.org).

Position: Operations and Compliance Analyst, Kathmandu, Nepal, NO-A
Job Identification: 36734
Apply Before: 09/30/2026, 11:59 PM
Job Schedule: Full time
Location: Kathmandu, Nepal
Grade: NOA
Vacancy Type: Fixed Term
Rotational/Non Rotational: Non-Rotational
Contract Duration: 1 Year with Possibility for extension
Required Languages: Fluency in oral and written English and national language of the duty station.

Job Description

The Position:

The Operations and Compliance Analyst provides support on financial management, assurance activities, and financial reporting and will provide dedicated operational support to facilitate the implementation and delivery of projects. The Position provides guidance, technical support, and oversight ensuring that resources are utilized appropriately and in compliance with relevant policies and requirements.

The selected candidate will be based at the UNFPA country office, Kathmandu, and will work under the guidance and direct supervision of the International Operations Manager. The Operations and Compliance Analyst will work closely with and will support UNFPA programme officers and the operations team, to ensure major risks and compliance are managed appropriately and programmes are implemented effectively.

How you can make a difference:

UNFPA is the lead United Nations agency for delivering a world where every pregnancy is intended, every childbirth is safe, and every young person’s potential is fulfilled. The UNFPA Strategic Plan for 2026-2029 articulates the organization’s response to a complex global environment, providing a roadmap for resilience and renewal. It is designed to accelerate the implementation of the Programme of Action of the International Conference on Population and Development (ICPD) and the achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals by 2030. This mandate is pursued through a focus on four interconnected outcomes: ending the unmet need for family planning; ending preventable maternal deaths; ending gender-based violence and harmful practices; and adapting to demographic change through evidence and rights-based policies.

In a world where fundamental human rights are at risk, we need principled and ethical staff who embody these international norms and standards and will defend them courageously and with full conviction.

UNFPA is seeking candidates who transform, inspire, and deliver high-impact sustained results, ensuring effective external relations, communications, partnership-building and resource mobilization in a rapidly changing development and funding landscape. We need staff who are transparent, exceptional in how they manage the resources entrusted to them, and who commit to delivering excellence in programme results

Job Purpose:

The position will play a supportive role for smooth running of financial, internal control, assurance, oversight, and audit functions ensuring compliance with corporate policies, rules, and regulations at all levels. Based on the close relationships built with internal and external stakeholders, the incumbent will assist the office to regularly communicate and support implementation of best practices in financial management and accountability tasks. The position will assist the office in budget and expenditure analysis, programme delivery monitoring, operational performance tracking, and management reporting to facilitate evidence-based planning, decision-making, and effective implementation of the country programme. The position will also support management decision-making through analysis of programme performance, operational trends, and compliance risks.

You would be responsible for:

Operational effectiveness, programme compliance, risk management, and quality assurance:

  • Support quality assurance reviews of compliance processes, including follow-up on audit recommendations, management responses and internal oversight findings.
  • Support in ERM related activities for the country office.
  • Support the development and implementation of oversight mechanisms for Country Office operations.
  • Support the assessment of the Internal Control Framework and assist in identifying internal control weaknesses, gaps, inefficiencies and overlaps.
  • Support the identification of deviations from established rules and regulations and bring them to the attention of the International Operations Manager for appropriate follow-up.
  • Support analysis of programme delivery, expenditure trends, implementation rates, and operational performance and provide inputs to identify bottlenecks and possible corrective actions.
  • Support in preparing periodic compliance, assurance, risk management, and operational performance reports and dashboards for Country Office management to support decision-making and strategic oversight.

Support to Implementing Partners Oversight and HACT assurance plan:

  • Support in conducting periodic due diligence for vetting of IPs.
  • Support the assessment of implementing partner risks and contribute to the identification of appropriate mitigation measures under the guidance of the International Operations Manager.
  • Assist in checking accuracy and validity of signatories and bank accounts in the IP agreement, with particular attention to high-risk management areas, such as sub-contracting, procurement, cash management.
  • Assist in the implementation of the approved HACT Assurance Plan under the guidance of the International Operations Manager.
  • Support the implementation of quarterly financial monitoring, in close coordination with relevant Programme Units and Area Offices and assist in validating the completion of programme activities as reported by IPs.
  • Support conduct spot checks and compliance reviews of IPs to ensure that financial, procurement and HR processes are in line with IPs established procedures and the requirements of HACT.
  • Support the review of audit reports and assist in documenting agreed follow-up actions in coordination with programme staff, implementing partners and auditors.
  • Support the review of findings from assessments, monitoring, verification, spot checks and audits, and assist in tracking follow-up actions and implementation of agreed mitigation measures.
  • Support in the regular updating of the United Nations Programme Portal (UNPP) platform by taking care of uploading all required documents and ensuring the quality of the information within it.

Programme Performance Monitoring and Financial Oversight:

  • Support to ensure alignment between approved cash limits and work plan budgets. Provide inputs from a finance and compliance perspective, supporting the accurate allocation of direct and indirect costs, and ensuring that all budgeted items reflect eligible expenditures in line with UNFPA financial guidelines.
  • Support the programme and finance team on timely and accurate review and clearance of work plans and eFace reports, ensuring compliance with UNFPA guidelines.
  • Support the finance team in the OFA reconciliation process avoiding negative OFAs at the end of the year.
  • Contributes to reviews, annual planning exercises, audits, and oversight processes through data analysis and operational reporting.
  • Support the development and maintenance of operational dashboards and tracking tools to strengthen accountability, transparency, and results-based management.

Performing Additional Duties as Assigned:

  • Carry out additional administrative and support tasks as required by UNFPA leadership.
  • Collaborates with team members, programme partners, and sub-grantees to ensure safe implementation of programmes at the community level applying Do No Harm approach.

Qualifications and Experience:

Education:

  • Advanced university degree in Finance/Accounting, Business, or Public Administration or a related field.

Knowledge and Experience:

  • Professional experience in finance or audit, or other directly related fields is advantageous.
  • Experience in the usage of computers and office software packages (MS Word, Excel, etc) and advanced knowledge of spreadsheet and database packages, experience in handling web-based management systems and ERP financials.
  • Prior experience in working with ERP systems (preferably Oracle based) is an advantage.
  • Previous experience in the UN and knowledge of UN internal control, risk management and implementing partner procedures is advantageous.
  • Excellent organizational skills, attention to detail, precision, and accuracy.
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills.
  • Should also possess the ability to formulate business requirements into logical system specifications.
  • Must be able to work in harmony across teams, both internally and externally.

Languages: Fluency in oral and written English and national language of the duty station.

Required Competencies:

Values:

  • Exemplifying integrity,
  • Demonstrating commitment to UNFPA and the UN system,
  • Embracing cultural diversity,
  • Embracing change.

Core Competencies:

  • Achieving results,
  • Being accountable,
  • Developing and applying professional expertise/business acumen,
  • Thinking analytically and strategically,
  • Working in teams/managing ourselves and our relationships,
  • Communicating for impact.

Functional Competencies:

  • Business acumen,
  • Implementing management systems,
  • Innovation and marketing of new approaches,
  • Client orientation,
  • Organizational awareness.

Compensation and Benefits:

This position offers an attractive remuneration package including a competitive net salary plus health insurance and other benefits as applicable.

UNFPA Work Environment:

UNFPA provides a work environment that reflects the values of gender equality, diversity, integrity and healthy work-life balance. We are committed to ensuring gender parity in the organization and therefore encourage women to apply. Individuals from the LGBTQIA+ community, minority ethnic groups, indigenous populations, persons with disabilities, and other underrepresented groups are highly encouraged to apply. Reasonable accommodation may be provided to applicants with disabilities upon request, to support their participation in the recruitment process. UNFPA promotes equal opportunities in terms of appointment, training, compensation and selection for all regardless of personal characteristics and dimensions of diversity. Diversity, Equity and Inclusion is at the heart of UNFPA’s workforce – click here to learn more.

Disclaimer:

Selection and appointment may be subject to background and reference checks, medical clearance, visa issuance and other administrative requirements.

UNFPA does not charge any application, processing, training, interviewing, testing or other fee in connection with the application or recruitment process and does not concern itself with information on applicants’ bank accounts.

  • Fixed Term, Full Time Role based in Kathmandu, Nepal.

ABOUT THE FRED HOLLOWS FOUNDATION

The Fred Hollows Foundation is an international development organisation working to prevent blindness and restore sight. We continue to carry on the legacy of Professor Fred Hollows, who believed every person had the right to quality eye care, no matter where they live. The Foundation is known around the world as an organisation that works with purpose and determination. With a reputation for excellence, we are well known for making change happen.

The Foundation has grown to work in more than 25+ countries throughout Africa, South Asia, Southeast Asia, the Middle East and the Pacific, as well as Australia. The Foundation has restored sight to more than 3 million people worldwide. We have an ambitious five-year strategic plan that aims to take us even closer to realising our vision of a world in which no person is needlessly blind, or vision impaired and Indigenous Australians exercise their right to sight and good health. To find out more about our work, please visit our website https://www.hollows.org

THE OPPORTUNITY

The Program Coordinator (PC) is accountable for the coordination, implementation, and monitoring of FHF Nepal project activities, working closely with the Nepal Eye Program – Tilganga Institute of Ophthalmology (TIO), regional partner hospitals, government stakeholders, and all other relevant stakeholders.

The PC will also support relevant components of the broader FHF Nepal project, ensuring alignment, collaboration, and evidence generation across multisectoral platforms. Based in Kathmandu, the role involves close coordination with TIO and government stakeholders, and may require domestic or international travel when needed.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Key areas of accountability include:

  • Coordinate day-to-day implementation of the FHF Nepal project, ensuring alignment with Nepal country strategy, project goals, and FHF values.
  • Develop project workplans and ensure timely, high-quality delivery of all project activities.
  • Support integration of eye health into the primary health system, in line with Nepal’s Government Eye Health Strategy.
  • Serve as the primary focal point for TIO, regional partner hospitals, government stakeholders, and other stakeholders.
  • Coordinate and maintain a multi-stakeholder steering committee, facilitating regular meetings and effective collaboration across partners.
  • Organise and support training activities with TIO, including training for a range of relevant participants.
  • Contribute to effective project implementation through regular, high-quality planning, implementation, monitoring, reporting, and evaluation.
  • Coordinate project financial and operational matters.
  • Prepare high-quality reports, including project updates, quarterly reports, field visit reports, donor reporting, and documentation for internal learning.
  • Identify, monitor, and mitigate risks related to project implementation, partnerships, worker participation, and operational challenges.

WHAT YOU’LL NEED TO SUCCEED

  • Experience working with INGOs and/or NGOs.
  • Proven ability to influence and build strong, collaborative working relationships with a wide network of partners and stakeholders, managing outcomes through those relationships.
  • Project management skills, with the ability to manage and juggle several projects concurrently.

HOW WE RECOGNISE YOUR CONTRIBUTION

Through our internal programs and employee benefits we aim to create an environment where you will feel supported and empowered.  Whether your focus is on continuous learning, professional development or finding an environment which enables you to thrive while balancing family or personal commitments, we have a range of programs in place to support you.

To find out more about our benefits click here

APPLICATIONS

Please apply directly using the “Apply” button. Your application should include a CV and, preferably, a cover letter that outlines your interest in the role and addresses the key criteria listed in the “Key Responsibilities”, and “What you need to succeed” sections of the advertisement.

Applications Close: Wednesday, 23 September 2026

BACKGROUND

Established in 1992, ANSAB is a non-profit, non-governmental organization committed to biodiversity conservation and livelihood improvement in Nepal. It places community empowerment and economic incentives at the heart of its approach and generates knowledge and results through applied research and studies to implement innovative solutions. ANSAB has been consistently evolving, consolidating, institutionalizing and advancing the approaches and strategies for the promotion of community-based enterprises and value chains, natural resources management and biodiversity conservation, enabling policy environment and multi-stakeholders.

ANSAB is urgently seeking to recruit a qualified, dynamic, and results-oriented individual for the position of Forest Officer under a project entitled “Scaling Conservation of Himalayan Plants and Fungi through Sustainable Trade”.

SCOPE OF WORK

The forest officer, based in Darchula, will be responsible for the efficient and timely execution of project activities at Darchula and Bajhang districts. Under the overall supervision of Senior Manager- Biodiversity and with day-to-day reporting to Field Program Coordinator, the Forest Officer will oversee and coordinate project activities in these two districts. It is important to note that this position requires excellent coordination skills and need frequent visits in the project working areas.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Liaise with district line agencies viz: Division Forest Offices, Park Offices, FECOFUN district chapters, NTFPs traders, trade associations, harvesters etc. for effective implementation of activities;
  • Organize and facilitate different surveys, assessments, researches, workshops, trainings and meetings in the district/s, including the exposure visits. Conduct if necessary;
  • Support and mobilize experts while conducting resource inventory of identified NTFPs;
  • Collect district level trade studies of selected NTFPs;
  • Capacitate and mobilize social mobilizers and Local Resource Persons (LRPs) within the district/s;
  • Analyze the gaps in CFUGs with respect to FairWild Certification standards;
  • Coordinate with CFUGs to (i) deliver trainings on organizational governance, sustainable harvesting, sustainable forest management to meet FairWild certification requirements; (ii) support to prepare and implement different management plans; (iii) provide technical support to identify, asses and manage high mountain herbs; and (iv) form sub-committees as required;
  • Provide support to existing and potential entrepreneurs on enterprise development, business skills, marketing, FairWild certification and associated document-management.

QUALIFICATION AND SKILLS

  • M.Sc. in Forestry, or M.Sc. in Natural Resource Management with a B.Sc. in Forestry, and at least one year of experience working in Himalayan districts;
  • Knowledge on community forestry, resource inventory, NTFPs and certification;
  • Excellent interpersonal and written communication skills in English and Nepali;
  • Ability to plan and prioritize work under pressure and tight deadlines;
  • Good computer skills including MS Word and Excel. Knowledge on GIS mapping will add value;
  • Motorbike riding skill with valid driving license.

DURATION AND LEVEL OF EFFORT

  • The duration of the engagement will be for two years, with possibility of extension.
  • Full-time position based in Darchula.

UNICEF works in over 190 countries and territories to save children’s lives, defend their rights, and help them fulfill their potential, from early childhood through adolescence.

At UNICEF, we are committed, passionate, and proud of what we do for as long as we are needed. Promoting the rights of every child is not just a job – it is a calling.

For every child, the right to Education

How can you make a difference?

UNICEF Nepal’s Education Section works with the Government of Nepal and development partners to improve access, equity, quality, governance and resilience in school education. The School Education Sector Plan (SESP) 2022-2032 is entering a decisive transition: a realistic and costed second five-year programme for 2027-2032 and a successor Joint Financing Arrangement must be developed while foundational learning, digitalization, inclusive education and federal service delivery are translated into practical sector arrangements. From August 2026, UNICEF serves as the Development Partner focal point, with the Embassy of Finland as co-focal point, creating a time-bound need for strong coordination, analysis, representation and follow-up. The role will also help inform the Local Education Development Partner Group of the work done through the Nepal Education Cluster in terms of the response and early-recovery work following the August 2026 floods.

Join UNICEF Nepal’s Education Section to support the country’s long-standing sector-wide approach at a decisive transition. You will help UNICEF in undertaking its Development Partner focal-point responsibilities, coordinate closely with the Ministry of Education and Sports and the Embassy of Finland, and connect sector dialogue with UNICEF programme and field evidence.

Your key functions and accountabilities will cover:

  • UNICEF core-team and focal-point coordination. Support planning, preparation and follow-up for UNICEF’s engagement with Government, Joint Financing Partners, LEDPG/LEG members and other stakeholders; maintain day-to-day coordination with MoES DACS and the Embassy of Finland; and prepare calendars, agendas, briefs, speaking points, meeting records, decision logs and action trackers.
  • Support to the second SESP programme (2027-2032). Coordinate UNICEF inputs to the Government-led roadmap, evidence review, consultations, drafting and decision calendar; promote foundational learning; facilitate meaningful federal, provincial and local consultation; and synthesize specialist inputs.
  • Support to the successor Joint Financing Arrangement. Organize UNICEF and partner contributions to the review and successor dialogue, improve the visibility of partner financing, coordinate specialist advice and maintain consultation records, comment matrices and action trackers.
  • Subnational participation and accountability. Help provincial education plans, Local Education Plans, budgets, implementation monitoring and frontline learning evidence inform federal dialogue, joint reviews and SESP II design.
  • Programme management, communication and risk management. Maintain an agreed workplan and milestones, provide decision-oriented analysis, identify and escalate risks, coordinate with UNICEF programme and operations colleagues and field offices, and undertake authorized official travel.
  • Education response and early recovery. Support regular updates to the LEDPG and coordination of response and early-recovery initiatives so that evidence and lessons from flood-affected areas inform joint sector reviews and planning.
  • If you would like to know more about this position, please review the complete Job Description here: Download File JD_Education Officer (Sector Coordination), NOB, TA, Kathmandu, Nepal #00138273.pdf

To qualify as an advocate for every child you will have…

Education: University degree (Bachelor’s) in education, public policy or administration, economics, development studies, social sciences or another relevant field is required.

Work Experience: Minimum two years of relevant professional experience in education programme planning, management, partnerships, coordination, policy support or a related area is required. Experience working with Government institutions and/or development partners and supporting multi-stakeholder processes, experience organizing high level external meetings or consultations, synthesizing evidence and diverse inputs, and preparing clear briefs, records or action trackers is required.   • Proficiency in Microsoft Word, Excel and PowerPoint and familiarity with collaborative document, virtual-meeting and knowledge-management tools.

Language Requirements: English and Nepali – Proficient/Fluent level is required.

Desirables:

  • Familiarity with Nepal’s SESP, SWAp, JFA, JRM/BRM, LEDPG/JFP processes, IEMIS or Local Education Plans will be an asset.

  •  Prior experience with UNICEF/UN or an international development institution is an asset.
  •  Knowledge of another official UN language is an asset.

For every Child, you demonstrate…

UNICEF’s Core Values of Care, Respect, Integrity, Trust and Accountability and Sustainability (CRITAS) underpin everything we do and how we do it. Get acquainted with Our Values Charter: UNICEF Values

Nepal Association of the Blind (NAB) is the national umbrella organization of blind and partially sighted people in Nepal. NAB works to promote the rights, inclusion, and empowerment of people with visual impairments through advocacy, capacity building, and service delivery. The Nepal Association of the Blind (NAB), with support from the Norwegian Association of Blind and Partially Sighted (NABP), is implementing Restoring Independence, a twelve-month disability-inclusive response to the August 2026 Bhote Koshi–Trishuli floods in Rasuwa, Nuwakot and Dhading. NAB invites applications from qualified Nepali citizens for the following position.

Major Responsibilities

  • Lead the planning, implementation, budgeting and quality assurance of the project, and supervise the project team.
  • Lead the accessible needs assessment, ensure disability-disaggregated data using the Washington Group Questions, and produce the assessment report for NDRRMA and NABP.
  • Oversee accessible referral, individual need-based support and community-based psychosocial counselling for persons with disabilities.
  • Represent NAB with NDRRMA, local governments, NFDN, local OPDs and the humanitarian clusters, and advocate for disability-inclusive help desks and an accessible disaster response hotline.

Required Qualifications

  • Demonstrated experience of disability inclusion, or of working with or within organizations of persons with disabilities.
  • Working knowledge of the UNCRPD, the Act Relating to Rights of Persons with Disabilities 2074, the Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Act 2074, and the IASC Guidelines on Inclusion of Persons with Disabilities in Humanitarian Action.
  • Excellent written and spoken Nepali and English, strong report writing and team management skills, and computer proficiency.
  • Willingness to travel and work in flood-affected areas under difficult conditions.
  • A valid driving license for a two-wheeler or four-wheeler will be an advantage/preference, given the frequent travel to flood-affected areas.
