The UN Secretary-General launched on 1 January 2019 a bold and new global reform which repositioned the UN Development System to deliver more effectively and efficiently the achievement of the 2030 Agenda and the Sustainable Development Goals. As part of this reform, UN Resident Coordinator Offices (UN RCO), under the leadership of an empowered and independent UN Resident Coordinator, support countries in the achievement of their development priorities and the attainment of the SDGs. The position is located in the United Nations Resident Coordination Office (RCO) in Kathmandu, Nepal. Under the direct supervision of the Head of Office and guidance of the RC and in full confidentiality, the Executive Assistant ensures effective and efficient functioning of the RC Front-Office, overall management of the RC’s schedule and logistical requirements, maintenance of protocol procedures, management of information flow, and follow-up on deadlines and commitments made.

Responsibilities

Within delegated authority, the Executive Assistant will be responsible for the following duties:

1. ENSURE EFFECTIVE AND EFFICIENT FUNCTIONING OF THE RC FRONT OFFICE FOCUSING ON ACHIEVEMENT OF THE FOLLOWING RESULTS:

  •  Maintain the Resident Coordinator’s calendar and representation schedule, arrange appointments and meetings of the RC, provide protocol coverage, ensure logistical details of RC participation in events, and act as an interpreter and/or taking minutes of meetings when required.
  •  Coordinate high-quality briefing materials for the RC for appointments, meetings, events, and missions and ensure that all correspondence and documents submitted to the RC are according to UN norms and standards including directives, coordinate comments on behalf of RC for signature and action/follow-up when required.
  •  Draft key correspondence, including notes to files, minutes of meetings and Note Verbales, and provide translation for official correspondence.
  • Prioritize tasks, meeting deadlines, and managing executive schedules effectively.
  • Anticipate issues and resolve them before they affect the executive’s work.
  • Manage RC travel and missions, prepare travel requests, ensure flight bookings and provision of logistics information, and follow up on trip reports and travel claims.
  • Maintain contact lists of high-level partners, UN Agencies, and Diplomatic Corps.
  •  Assist in organizing official events: travel (booking flights, request for security clearance, arrangements at airport, etc.) for local and high-level visitors as required.
  •  In collaboration with the RCO team, prepare and maintain checklists and templates for relevant processes (high level visits, meetings preparation etc).
  •  Provide all similar services and support to RC a.i.
  •  Remain effective in fast-changing environments and shifting priorities.
  •  Act as a trusted partner who anticipates needs and helps executives stay focused on priorities.

2. ENSURE PROVISION OF EFFECTIVE COMMUNICATIONS SUPPORT TO THE OFFICE FOCUSING ON THE ACHIEVEMENT OF THE FOLLOWING RESULTS:

  • Demonstrated ability to communicate clearly, professionally, and effectively, both orally and in writing, with internal and external stakeholders at all levels.
  • Handle sensitive information with professionalism and trustworthiness.
  • Have proven track record of strong working relationships with government and other external partners including ability to build strong relationships with colleagues, especially decision makers.
  • Maintain the filing system (in TEAMS/Sharepoint) ensuring safekeeping of confidential materials. Use of automated filing system.
  •  Screen RC incoming calls and correspondence.
  • Demonstrate ability to use AI, Strong skills in Microsoft 365, Teams, Outlook, Excel, PowerPoint, and collaboration tools.
  • Coordinate the activities of the RC driver.
  •  Support organize and communicate on the various coordination meetings, including UNCT Meetings.
  • Participate in the organization of official UN Days, public events, joint UN events and provide secretariat and administrative support to the UNCT
  • Follow up on deadlines, commitments made, actions taken and coordination of collection and submission of the reports to RC.

3. HUMAN RESOURCES MANAGEMENT:

  • Provide support to the RC in matters such as documentation, visas, travel arrangements, house and school search, etc.

4. OFFICE ADMINISTRATION:

  • Act as an alternate to the RCO Administrative Assistant when required to support RCO in day to-day administrative tasks as required, including contract administration, budget and finance, and human resource management.
  •  Assists with the collection and analysis of data as well as preparation of data presentations and reports for information sharing, responding to queries, knowledge management, planning and decision making.
  •  Assists with visualizations and updating information material such as web pages or brochures.
  •  Ensures that requirements and background information used for data analysis are documented.
  • Performs other relevant duties as assigned.

Competencies

Professionalism:

Ability to perform a broad range of administrative functions, e.g., budget/work programme, human resources, database management, etc.

Ability to apply knowledge of various United Nations administrative, financial and human resources rules and regulations in work situations.
Ability to apply sustainable development theories, concepts and approaches.
Ability to conduct independent research and analysis on sustainable development topics, determine suitability, validity and accuracy of data provided by different sources.
Shows skill in developing sources for data collection.
Shows pride in work and in achievements; demonstrates professional competence and mastery of subject matter; is conscientious and efficient in meeting commitments, observing deadlines and achieving results; is motivated by professional rather than personal concerns; shows persistence when faced with difficult problems or challenges; remains calm in stressful situations; commitment to implementing the goal of gender equality by ensuring the equal participation and full involvement of women and men in all aspects of work.

Communication: Speaks and writes clearly and effectively; listens to others, correctly interprets messages from others and responds appropriately; asks questions to clarify, and exhibits interest in having two-way communication; tailors language, tone, style and format to match audience; demonstrates openness In sharing information and keeping people informed.

Teamwork: Works collaboratively with colleagues to achieve organizational goals; solicits input by genuinely valuing others’ ideas and expertise; is willing to learn from others; places team agenda before personal agenda; supports and acts in accordance with final group decision, even when such decisions may not entirely reflect own position; shares credit for team accomplishments and accepts joint responsibility for team shortcomings.

Education

  • Completion of a High school diploma or equivalent is required. Bachelors or advanced university degree in business administration, office management, communication or related fields would be an advantage.

Work Experience

  • A minimum of seven (7) years of experience in administrative support, coordination, logistics or front office functions is required.
  • The minimum years of relevant experience is reduced by two (2) years for candidates who possess a first level University degree.
  • Demonstrated experience in supporting senior officials or executive offices, including protocol arrangements is desirable.
  • Demonstrated experience in organizing meetings, missions and high-level events, including coordination with internal and external stakeholders is desirable.
  • Work experience with the United Nations, international organization, diplomatic mission or government institution is desirable.
  • One(1) year or more of experience in data analytics or related area is desirable.

Job Description:

Key Responsibilities:

1. Internal Inventory Management

Oversee and manage the inventory of laboratory supplies, reagents, and equipment, ensuring stock levels are maintained and efficiently utilized to prevent shortages of overstocking.

2. Instrument and Reagent Optimization

Ensure optimal utilization of laboratory instruments and reagents to maximize efficiency and minimize waste, while maintaining the accuracy and quality of test results.

3. NABL (ISO 15189:2022) Compliance

Conduct and maintain laboratory practices in strict adherence to NABL (ISO 15189:2022) standards, ensuring that all processes, documentation, and operations meet accreditation requirements.

4.Quality Control and Assurance

Implement and monitor quality control procedures, including performing daily internal control runs and analyzing Levey-Jennings (LJ) curves. Take corrective actions when needed and document all steps to ensure accurate and reliable test results.

5. Turnaround Time (TAT) Management

Monitor and manage the turnaround time (TAT) for all laboratory services, ensuring timely processing, analysis, and reporting of test results to maintain operational efficiency.

6. Equipment Maintenance and Troubleshooting

Conduct daily maintenance of laboratory instruments, perform necessary repairs, and ensure timely validation to prevent malfunctions. Document maintenance activities and address issues promptly.

7. Data Management and Documentation

Accurately record and manage test results, ensuring that comprehensive and organized documentation is maintained in line with regulatory and organizational standards, including recording re-runs and corrective actions taken.

8. Training and Mentorship

Provide training and guidance to junior staff and interns, ensuring they are well-versed in laboratory procedures, quality control practices, and safety protocols.

9. Staff Management and Duty Rosters

Manage duty rosters for lab staff to ensure adequate coverage, maintain smooth workflow, and promote a positive working environment that fosters teamwork, communication, and high morale.

10. Lab Operations Management

Oversee the overall management of the lab, ensuring smooth day-to-day operations.

Resolve any issues that arise while promoting continuous improvement and enhancing patient engagement and service utilization.

11. Patient Interaction

When necessary, interact with patients to collect samples, provide clear instructions, ensure their comfort during procedures, and offer post-report counseling as needed.

12. Safety and Regulatory Compliance

Adhere to all safety guidelines and regulations, ensuring a safe working environment for all laboratory personnel while maintaining compliance with health and safety standards.

13. Quality System Improvement

Recommend improvements to the quality management system and testing kits to the Head of Department (HOD) for better performance, accuracy, and patient care.

14. Analytics and Management Reporting

Analyze lab performance data, including test volumes, error rates, and TAT. Prepare regular management reports on key performance indicators (KPIs), financial metrics, and quality improvement initiatives. Use data-driven insights to enhance lab efficiency and decision-making. Report to management on weekly basis.

15. Budget Management

Assist in managing the lab’s budget, ensuring optimal allocation of resources, controlling expenses, and contributing to the financial health of the department.

16. External Vendor and Supplier Management

Liaise with external suppliers and service providers for equipment procurement, reagent supplies, and outsourced services. Negotiate contracts and ensure timely deliveries while maintaining quality and cost-effectiveness.

17. Audit Preparation and Compliance

Coordinate with internal and external auditors to prepare for laboratory audits. Ensure all documentation and processes meet the required standards for NABL and ISO compliance.

18. Strategic Planning and Development

Contribute to the strategic planning of the laboratory by identifying new technologies, methodologies, and services that can enhance lab performance and patient care. Assist in long-term goal setting and resource planning.

Position: Induction Furnace Manager
Location: Pokhariya, Birgunj, Parsa, Narayani, Nepal
Reports to: Head – Meltshop

Role Summary

The Induction Furnace Manager owns the complete performance of the Steel Melting Shop (SMS) induction furnace operations, from heat planning to tapping, ensuring consistent achievement of production targets, optimal power consumption, and strict metallurgical quality control.
This role demands a hands-on leader capable of setting up disciplined furnace operations, stabilizing processes, and driving efficiency in a greenfield/startup plant environment. The incumbent will play a critical role in building systems, training teams, and establishing benchmarks for productivity, cost, and safety.

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead end-to-end induction furnace operations, including melting, refining, and tapping cycles
  •  Develop and execute heat plans, tapping schedules, and furnace campaign strategies
  •  Drive power panel optimization to achieve best-in-class energy consumption (kWh/tonne)
  • Ensure precise alloy addition control to meet required chemistry and minimize rework
  •  Oversee charge mix optimization (scrap, sponge iron, alloys) to improve yield and reduce cost
  •  Manage refractory lifecycle, including lining practices, performance monitoring, and procurement
  •  Coordinate closely with charge preparation, maintenance, and quality teams for seamless operations
  • Lead shift scheduling, manpower deployment, and productivity management on the shop floor
  •  Troubleshoot electrical, mechanical, and process issues affecting furnace performance
  •  Establish and monitor process control parameters including temperature, slag chemistry, and melt time
  • Drive continuous improvement initiatives to reduce downtime, improve yield, and stabilize operations
  •  Ensure strict adherence to safety standards and incident prevention protocols
  •  Maintain accurate production reporting, heat logs, and performance analysis

Technical Expertise Required

  •  Strong hands-on experience in induction furnace operations (medium/high frequency)
  • Deep understanding of metallurgy: scrap behavior, alloying, slag control, and temperature management
  •  Proven track record in power consumption optimization (kWh/tonne reduction)
  •  Expertise in refractory management, lining practices, and campaign life improvement
  •  Knowledge of furnace power systems and panel operations
  • Experience in charge mix design and yield improvement techniques
  • Familiarity with pollution control and compliance norms in SMS operations

Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

  • Achievement of daily induction furnace production targets
  • Power consumption (kWh per tonne)
  • Refractory cost per tonne and campaign life
  •  Chemistry compliance rate (first-time right heats)
  •  Tapping temperature accuracy
  • Reduction in downtime and process deviations
  • Improvement in yield and material efficiency

Minimum Qualifications & Experience

  • B.Tech in Metallurgy (preferred) or relevant engineering discipline
  • Minimum 10 years of hands-on experience in induction furnace operations
  •  Strong experience in:
    o Refractory management
    o Charge mix optimization
    o Meltshop process control
  • Prior exposure to plant setup, commissioning, or startup operations will be a strong advantage

Leadership Expectations

  •  Strong shop-floor ownership with a bias for action
  • Ability to build, train, and lead teams from the ground up
  •  Decisive problem-solving in high-pressure production environments
  •  High accountability for output, cost, quality, and safety metrics
  •  Willingness to work in a startup plant setup with evolving systems and processes

What We Are Looking For

A results-driven furnace expert who doesn’t just manage operations but builds and stabilizes them—someone who understands the realities of the shop floor, can optimize every heat, and is committed to delivering consistent performance from day one.

Interested candidates may send their CV to: hr@primesteel.com.np

Posiiton: Field Coordinator (0pen to Nepalese Nationals Only)
Location: Butwal, Lumbini Province

Description

iDE is an international nonprofit organisation dedicated to ending poverty. Our work in agriculture, sanitation, climate change resilience, and gender equality stands out because we don’t simply hand out handouts. Instead, iDE believes in powering small-scale entrepreneurs and building robust market ecosystems that lay the groundwork for low-income and marginalised people to prosper on their own terms. iDE currently works in 11 developing countries, with over 500 staff spread around the globe. To date, iDE has impacted more than 40 million people.

Since 1992, iDE Nepal has been actively fostering prosperity by establishing value chains and innovative business models in key sectors, including agriculture, nutrition, market systems development, water and sanitation, climate resilience, and gender equality. Our approach aims to catalyse the development of beneficial, cost-effective products and services that contribute to sustainable growth and enhanced well-being. Our long-standing presence in Nepal is a testimony to adaptive learning, continual innovation, and commitment to delivering meaningful impact. iDE Nepal’s holistic approach to market development is what truly sets us apart.

Building on this experience and expertise, iDE Nepal is seeking a leader who can translate its market-based approach to nutrition into strategic, high-quality implementation and sustainable impact across the region.This position will provide overall strategic, technical, and operational leadership for the Transforming Lives through Nutrition (Transforming Lives) Project, implemented in Dang, Nawalparasi West, Kapilvastu, and Rupandehi Districts. The position will also support implementation of future projects in the region.

He/She will lead the field team, strengthen the capacity of implementing partners, and represent iDE Nepal in relevant forums. The role will ensure effective project implementation, field coordination, monitoring, learning, reporting, and partner support, while maintaining quality, compliance, and achievement of project results. The position will provide technical leadership on nutrition-sensitive and climate-resilient food systems, strengthen private-sector and government partnerships, and promote innovative, scalable, and market-based solutions. Using iDE’s Market Systems Development approach, the position will support outcomes across nutrition, food security, climate-smart agriculture, and WASH, while generating evidence and learning to inform future programming and scale. The position will be based in Butwal, with frequent travel to project locations.

Key Responsibilities

Planning , Management, and Representation

  • Provide strategic leadership and technical support for effective project management and delivery, ensuring quality, compliance, and alignment with organizational priorities.
  • Lead project planning, including development of DIPs, implementation guidelines, operational plans, and adaptive management in response to changing contexts.
  • Ensure integration of GESI, risk management, safeguarding, and other organizational standards across project implementation.
  • Coordinate closely with project, technical/thematic, partner, and Country Office teams to ensure effective implementation and timely resolution of operational issues.
  • Build and maintain effective relationships with government, private sector, development partners, community stakeholders, and other relevant actors, and represent iDE Nepal in key forums and events.
  • Ensure effective communication and coordination with relevant stakeholders and promote collaboration, learning, and resource sharing across the region.

Team Management

  • Provide leadership, guidance, and performance management to team members, ensuring clear roles, accountability, and alignment with organizational objectives.
  • Assess staffing and capacity-building needs and work with HR, line managers, and technical leads to strengthen team capacity and performance.
  • Coordinate team planning, workload, and resource allocation to ensure efficient and effective delivery of project activities.
  • Support staff development, performance appraisal, and resolution of team-related issues in coordination with the Country Office.

Monitoring, Reporting and Learning

Posiiton: Monitoring and Evaluation Officer (0pen to Nepalese National Only)

Description

iDE is an international nonprofit organisation dedicated to ending poverty. Our work in agriculture, sanitation, climate change resilience, and gender equality stands out because we don’t simply hand out handouts. Instead, iDE believes in powering small-scale entrepreneurs and building robust market ecosystems that lay the groundwork for low-income and marginalised people to prosper on their own terms. iDE currently works in 11 developing countries, with over 500 staff spread around the globe. To date, iDE has impacted more than 40 million people.

Since 1992, iDE Nepal has been actively fostering prosperity by establishing value chains and innovative business models in key sectors, including agriculture, nutrition, market systems development, water and sanitation, climate resilience, and gender equality. Our approach aims to catalyse the development of beneficial, cost-effective products and services that contribute to sustainable growth and enhanced well-being. Our long-standing presence in Nepal is a testimony to adaptive learning, continual innovation, and commitment to delivering meaningful impact. iDE Nepal’s holistic approach to market development is what truly sets us apart.

The Monitoring and Evaluation Officer will play a crucial role in the efficient and effective management of the monitoring and evaluation aspects of the overall iDE project in the region. Based in Kathmandu, his role involves leading regional-level reporting, monitoring, and evaluation activities.

Leading and managing team to deliver project activities in the M & E component:

  • Supervise, mentor and guide field M&E staff, monitor and follow up on field-level project activities to ensure accurate reporting.
  • Prepare project reports and keep databases as per standards formats and as per need.
  • Facilitate and support the district/field team for the reporting of progress on activities as planned in the Detail Implementation Plan (DIP) in close coordination with other concerned project staff.
  • Develop and update monitoring tools based on the reporting needs provided by the M&E lead.
  • Facilitate to develop capacity of project and partner staff on data collection and reporting.
  • Technical backstopping to project staff on effective and timely reporting of project activities.
  • Follow the M & E reporting and documentation requirements and donor guidelines.
  • Provide feedback to the district team for quality reports and achieve project targets in time.
  • Support to develop action plans and strategies.
  • Represent the iDE proactively in different M & E related for a (meetings, sharing events etc.) as necessary.
  • Provide support and maintenance to existing MIS systems and maintain documentation for smooth operation and easy system maintenance.
  • Responsible for overseeing the TLTN project, ensuring its timely completion within budget and scope while adhering to MERL’s quality standards.
  • Any other duties as assigned by the organisation.

Additional specific elements of the ToR include:

  • Closely work with all concerned officials and concerned personnel to consolidate reports.
  • Participate in M & E related activities and other relevant activities at different levels.
  • Supervise and guide the monitoring officer field staff, follow up and monitor the field level project activities frequently so that reporting would reflect reality.
  • Prepare and deliver progress reports monthly, quarterly, half yearly and annually as per need of M & E reporting system.
  • Ensure that the reporting made by the staff accurately meets the reporting deadline and quality standard.
  • Oversee and make sure that the information required for M & E and project implementation are properly collected, processed and documented.
  • Develop, implement, and maintain data protection policies and practices to safeguard personal data.
  • Integrate evidence-based decision-making system by the systematic collection, analysis, and application of relevant data to guide all key decisions.
  • Other jobs and duties related to M & E as directed by the MERL Leader and other concerned senior projects dignitaries.

Requirements

  • Bachelor with 3 years’ experience. Master Degree with a 2 year experience. (Background: Agriculture Economic (Preferred), Sociology, Business Studies or other)
  • Experience in delivering field-level extension activities, organising training, and training received in agriculture, nutrition, and food loss related subjects.
  • Experience working in the agriculture and nutrition sector with a market systems development approach
  • Experience in post harvest, food loss and waste reduction as well in research projects will be an added benefit.

Posiiton: District Coordinator

The Organisation

Plan International is an independent development and humanitarian organisation that advances children’s rights and equality for girls. We believe in the power and potential of every child but know this is often suppressed by poverty, violence, exclusion and discrimination. And it is girls who are most affected.

Working together with children, young people, supporters and partners, we strive for a just world, tackling the root causes of the challenges girls and vulnerable children face. We support children’s rights from birth until they reach adulthood and we enable children to prepare for and respond to crises and adversity. We drive changes in practice and policy at local, national and global levels using our reach, experience and knowledge.

For over 85 years, we have rallied other determined optimists to transform the lives of all children in more than 80 countries.

We won’t stop until we are all equal.

ROLE PURPOSE

Plan International is a development and humanitarian organization that advances children’s rights and equality for girls. We strive for a just world, working together with children, young people, our supporters and partners in over 75 countries. Our programs are underpinned by a core of defined values, including transparency and accountability, team collaboration, inclusion and integration, as well as the overall ambition to empower girls and young women as legacy.

Plan International has been working in Nepal since 1978 and developed a strong reputation as a respected development and humanitarian actor helping marginalized children, their families and communities to access their rights to health, education, economic security and protection. Through the support of local partners, Plan International has worked in 42 districts in Nepal since 1978.

Plan International strives for a just world that advances children’s rights and equality for girls. Our ambition from now to 2027 is to see All Girls Standing Strong Creating Global Change.

Plan international Nepal seeks candidates who practice feminist leadership, promote diversity, actively seek innovative solutions for problems, courageously and respectfully share their opinions and ideas, break down barriers and engender cross-department collaboration, practice active.

Plan International’s global strategy applies a full spectrum approach where Disaster Risk Management (DRM) is an integral part of everything the organisation does for children and girls, especially in fragile settings. A new DRM vision was developed in 2018 highlighting Plan’s ambition of becoming a global leader and the NGO partner of choice for promoting gender equality and protecting girls’ rights in disaster and conflict settings, working at the nexus of development and humanitarian efforts.

Plan International has over the last 15 years developed a significant DRM portfolio and focused its efforts on both mainstreaming DRM within its long-term development programmes as well as building the necessary disaster preparedness and response capacity across the organization to ensure the delivery of timely and appropriate programmatic responses to crisis as per sector quality standards, The Core Humanitarian Standards, (CHS).

As District Coordinator for Nepal Flash Floods you will be responsible for overall implementation of project activities in Nuwakot. You will required to support the emergency responses activities at the field level by capacitating Plan as well as Partner Staff for smooth implementation.

Dimensions of the Role

The post holder will ensure all project activities are implemented in the project area with quality and on time. The position holder is responsible to work closely with the Partners and other stakeholders for smooth implementation and coordinate day to day operations at District level.

The post holder will work with operational support departments (Finance, Logistics & Procurement, People & Culture, Fundraising, Security, IT, Systems) to support integration of emergency response in to standard tools, guidance and systems.

The role will represent Plan International in relevant external fora and inter-agency coordination groups at the District level.

Responsibility for upholding and implementing relevant aspects of all Plan policies and procedures, including the ‘Say Yes! To Keeping Children Safe’ Policy.

Accountabilities

1. District Coordination and Stakeholder Engagement

  • Establish and maintain effective coordination with relevant district authorities, government line agencies, local stakeholders, and other relevant actors.
  • Facilitate regular coordination meetings and information-sharing related to project implementation.
  • Represent the project at relevant district-level coordination forums, as appropriate.
  • Identify emerging implementation issues and facilitate timely resolution in coordination with relevant stakeholders.

2. Partner Support and Implementation Oversight

  • Provide regular technical and operational support to implementing partners to facilitate effective project delivery.
  • Monitor partner implementation against approved plans, targets, timelines, budgets, and agreed quality standards.
  • Conduct regular field visits and monitoring to assess progress, identify gaps, and provide constructive feedback.
  • Follow up on agreed actions and ensure timely implementation of recommendations.
  • Support partners in identifying and addressing operational, technical, and contextual challenges.

3. Quality Assurance and Compliance

  • Ensure project implementation is aligned with approved project documents, organisational policies, donor requirements, and relevant government standards.
  • Monitor compliance with donor and internal requirements throughout implementation.
  • Strengthen documentation, reporting, and evidence of project activities and results.
  • Identify compliance and quality risks and work with partners and relevant internal teams to address them.
  • Contribute to periodic project reviews, assessments, reporting, and learning processes.

4. Complaint Handling and Feedback Mechanism

  • Operationalise and strengthen the project’s Complaint Handling and Feedback Mechanism at district and community levels.
  • Ensure project participants are aware of available channels for providing feedback, raising complaints, and reporting concerns.
  • Ensure complaints and feedback are recorded, referred, followed up, and closed in a timely, confidential, and appropriate manner.
  • Monitor trends and recurring issues from feedback and complaints and support programme improvements based on findings.
  • Ensure that feedback mechanisms are accessible, inclusive, safe, and appropriate for different groups of project participants.

5. Safeguarding and Protection of Project Participants

  • Strengthen safeguarding measures throughout project implementation and partner engagement.
  • Ensure partners and project teams understand and comply with relevant safeguarding, Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA), Child Safeguarding, and other applicable organisational standards.
  • Promote safe, dignified, inclusive, and do-no-harm approaches in project activities.
  • Support identification and mitigation of safeguarding risks associated with project implementation.
  • Ensure safeguarding concerns are handled through appropriate reporting and referral mechanisms, maintaining confidentiality and survivor-centred approaches.
  • Promote awareness among project participants, partners, and staff regarding their rights and available safeguarding and reporting channels.
  • Ensure that Plan International’s global policies for Safeguarding Children and Young People and Gender Equality and Inclusion are fully embedded in accordance with the principles and requirements of the policy including relevant implementation standards and guidelines as applicable to area of responsibility. Including, but not limited to, ensuring staff and associates are aware of and understand their responsibilities under these policies and Plan International’s Code of Conduct (CoC); relevance to area of work, and concerns are reported and managed in accordance with the appropriate procedures

Key relationships

Internally:

  • Works closely with Programmes, Partner Management and Impact, Programme Quality and Innovation, Business Development, Operations and Finance teams
  • Senior Technical Advisor- Disaster RisK Management & Climate Change Adaptation and Humanitarian Response Manager at country office and Direct reports to Emergency Response Manager
  • National Organisation disaster risk management network

Externally:

  • Interagency working groups and coordination fora.

Technical expertise, skills and knowledge

  • Master’s Degree in relevant field with minimum 3 years of proven experience working in a similar portfolio or 5 years’ experience with a Bachelor’s degree
  • Demonstrable experience of developing and leading gender responsive humanitarian programming.
  • Broad knowledge of the humanitarian sector
  • Thorough knowledge of the programme and operations dimensions of implementing emergency responses;
  • Must be fluent in English and Nepali
  • Significant experience of leading emergency response operations.
  • Demonstrable experience of humanitarian standards (Sphere, CHS etc)
  • Creative approach to problem solving is central to the job.
  • Experience of developing and conducting capacity building programmes.
  • Flexibility to adapt plans to a changing environment
  • Developing and maintaining collaborative relationships; managing self in a pressured and changing environment; motivating and influencing others
  • Adherence to humanitarian values and standards
  • Actively takes steps to uphold Plan International’s vision, values and behaviours and policies, including the Say Yes! To Keeping Children Safe Policy.

Plan International’s Values in Practice

We are open and accountable

We create a climate of trust inside and outside the organisation by being open, honest and transparent. We hold ourselves and others to account for the decisions we make and for our impact on others, while doing what we say we will do.

We strive for lasting impact
We strive to achieve significant and lasting impact on the lives of children and young people, and to secure equality for girls. We challenge ourselves to be bold, courageous, responsive, focused and innovative.

We work well together
We succeed by working effectively with others, inside and outside the organisation, including our sponsors and donors. We actively support our colleagues, helping them to achieve their goals. We come together to create and implement solutions in our teams, across Plan International, with children, girls, young people, communities and our partners.

We are inclusive and empowering
We respect all people, appreciate differences and challenge inequality in our programmes and our workplace. We support children, girls and young people to increase their confidence and to change their own lives. We empower our staff to give their best and develop their potential.

Physical Environment

The position holder will be based in Nuwakot.

Level of contact with children

Mid contact: Occasional interaction with children

Location: Field Office- Nuwakot

Type of Role: Short-term (6 months)

Reports to: Emergency Response Specialist

Grade: C2

Closing Date: 17 September 2026

Equality, diversity and inclusion is at the very heart of everything that Plan International stands for.

We want Plan International to reflect the diversity of the communities we work with, offering equal opportunities to everyone regardless of age, disability, gender reassignment, marriage and civil partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race, religion or belief, sex or sexual orientation.

Plan International is based on a culture of inclusivity and we strive to create a workplace environment that ensures every team, in every office, in every country, is rich in diverse people, thoughts, and ideas.

We foster an organisational culture that embraces our commitment to racial justice, gender equality, girls’ rights and inclusion.

Plan International believes that in a world where children face so many threats of harm, it is our duty to ensure that we, as an organisation, do everything we can to keep children safe. This means that we have particular responsibilities to children that we come into contact with and we must not contribute in any way to harming or placing children at risk.

A range of pre-employment checks will be undertaken in conformity with Plan International’s Safeguarding Children and Young People policy. Plan International also participates in the Inter Agency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme. In line with this scheme we will request information from applicants previous employers about any findings of sexual exploitation, sexual abuse and/or sexual harassment during employment, or incidents under investigation when the applicant left employment. By submitting an application, the job applicant confirms their understanding of these recruitment procedures.

Please note that Plan International will never send unsolicited emails requesting payment from candidates.

The National Federation of Women Living with HIV and AIDS (NFWLHA), formerly known as the Women’s Network against HIV & AIDS (WONAHA), was initially established as a loose network in 2006 and was officially registered in 2007 with a vision to create a just and equitable society for women and children infected and affected with HIV, so that they can live a productive, empowered and dignified life, free from stigma and discrimination. Underpinned by guiding principles of gender equity and human rights, evidence-based planning, programming, and policy advocacy, NFWLHA has broadened its strategic intervention areas over the last nine years, focusing mainly on strengthening and capacity development of the network, knowledge management for evidence-based policy advocacy and community system strengthening. Currently, there are 35 community-based organizations (CBOs) affiliated with NFWLHA representing Nepal’s seven provinces, all led by women living with HIV (WLHIV).

JOB TITLE: Information & Communications Coordinator
TEAM/PROGRAMME: Program Operation Department
LOCATION: Nuwakot
GRADE: 3
Contract Type: 6 Months, with possible of extension

Child Safeguarding Level 3 – the responsibilities of the post holder may require having a regular contact with or access to children or young people because the position holder works in the implementation of the country programme and are visiting programme frequently.

ROLE PURPOSE:

Save the Children is the leading independent organization for children. We save children’s lives; we fight for their rights; we help them fulfill their potential. We work together, with our partners from civil society and government, to inspire breakthroughs in the way the world treats children and to achieve immediate and lasting change in their lives.

The Information and Communications Coordinator will support the flood response operation by ensuring the timely collection, verification, consolidation, and dissemination of accurate field information. The position will function as a critical link between field teams and the media and communications team in the Country Office to facilitate quality reporting, and effective public communications. The position will ensure that all information and communications products adhere to organizational safeguarding, consent, dignity, and media standards.

SCOPE OF ROLE:

Position reports to: Field Operations Lead

Technical reporting to: Communications and Campaigns Manager

Staff directly reporting to this post: None.

Staff indirectly reporting to this post: None.

Scheme of Delegation:

Close coordination with:

Budget Responsibility:

KEY AREAS OF ACCOUNTABILITY:

  • Generate, compile, analyze, and consolidate information for daily Situation Reports (SitReps) and other operational updates.
  • Collect and verify response data from field teams, partners, and relevant stakeholders to ensure accuracy and consistency.
  • Maintain organized records of response activities, beneficiary reach, key achievements, challenges, and emerging needs.
  • Gather and document high-quality photos, videos, beneficiary stories, testimonials, and human-interest content showcasing response efforts and community impact.
  • Ensure field information is collected using approved tools, formats, and reporting templates.
  • Support the Media & Communications Coordinator with developing, updating and finalising FAQs, key messages and briefing materials.
  • Verify information from multiple sources before sharing with internal and external stakeholders.
  • Ensure all communications materials, photos, videos, interviews, and stories meet organizational safeguarding, consent, dignity, and media standards.
  • Verify that informed consent has been obtained and documented prior to collecting or sharing personal information, images, or testimonials.
  • Ensure sensitive information is handled appropriately and in accordance with data protection requirements and SCI’s communications principles
  • Ensure adherence to SCI’s branding and visibility standards for all materials in the field office
  • Promote ethical storytelling practices that respect the rights, privacy, and dignity of affected individuals and communities.
  • Participate in field coordination meetings and provide timely information updates to response teams.
  • Support the field office technical coordinators in developing SBC materials for WASH promotion activities in consultation with the PDQI department
  • Represent SCI in relevant cluster meetings, technical working groups, and coordination forums as assigned by the Field Operations Lead.
  • Share project updates, challenges, and achievements with relevant stakeholders.
  • Ensure data and the information from the field are regularly updated to the relevant teams and departments in the Country Office.
  • Comply with Save the Children policies and practice with respect to child protection, code of conduct, health and safety, equal opportunities and other relevant policies and procedures.

Counter Fraud and Safeguarding Responsibilities:

  • Take all necessary and appropriate steps to prevent abuse, exploitation, neglect, harm and modern slavery within their areas of responsibility, and in the way they conduct themselves, report and respond to all incidents and concerns whether online or in person, and comply with the Safeguarding Policy and Procedure.
  • Take all necessary and appropriate steps to prevent fraud, bribery, and corruption within their areas of responsibility, report and respond to all incidents and concerns and comply with the Counter-Fraud, Bribery and Corruption Policy and Procedure. All types of fraud, bribery, and corruption must be prevented, including where it benefits the organisation (SCI).

SKILLS AND BEHAVIOURS (our Values in Practice)

Accountability:

  • Holds self-accountable for making decisions, managing resources efficiently, achieving and role modelling Save the Children values
  • Holds the team and partners accountable to deliver on their responsibilities – giving them the freedom to deliver in the best way they see fit, providing the necessary development to improve performance and applying appropriate consequences when results are not achieved
  • Sets ambitious and challenging goals for themselves and their team, takes responsibility for their own personal development and encourages others to do the same
  • Widely shares their personal vision for Save the Children, engages and motivates others
  • Future orientated, thinks strategically.
  • Builds and maintains effective relationships, with their team, colleagues, Members and external partners and supporters
  • Values diversity, sees it as a source of competitive strength
  • Approachable, good listener, easy to talk to
  • Develops and encourages new and innovative solutions
  • Willing to take disciplined risks
  • Honest, encourages openness and transparency

Ambition:

Collaboration:

Creativity:

Integrity:

QUALIFICATION:

  • A minimum of 3 years’ (2 years for GSI ) experience in communications, humanitarian response, information management, or related areas with the Master degree in communications/journalism/social science or relevant areas or 5 years ( 3 years for GSI group) of experience in communications, humanitarian response, information management, or related areas with bachelor’s degree in communications/journalism/social science or relevant areas

EXPERIENCE AND SKILLS

  • Experience collecting, analyzing, and reporting field data during humanitarian or disaster response operations.
  • Proven experience developing communication content, including stories, photographs, videos, and situation reports. Strong reporting, facilitation, and communication skills.
  • Ability to travel extensively to flood-affected and remote locations.
  • Fluency in English and Nepali, both written and spoken
  • Ability to collect and verify information under tight deadlines.
  • Commitment to the aims and principles of SCI in particular, a good understanding of the SCI mandate and child focus and an ability to ensure this continues to underpin our support
  • Ability to establish good working relationships and positively contribute to a team
  • Ability to work in a stressful and changing environment with limited resources

Additional Job Responsibilities:

The duties and responsibilities as set out above are not exhaustive and the role holder may be required to carry out additional duties within reasonableness of their level of skills and experience.

Equal Opportunities:

The role holder is required to carry out the duties in accordance with the SCI Equal Opportunities and Diversity policies and procedures.

Safeguarding obligation:

We need to keep children, adult at risk and community safe. The position holder is responsible to ensure that The position holder conduct is in line with the SCI’s Safeguarding policies. Hence our selection process includes rigorous background checks, reflects our commitment to the protection of children, adult at risk and community from abuse, exploitation, and harassment.

Health and Safety:

The role holder is required to carry out the duties in accordance with SCI Health and Safety policies and procedures.

Safeguarding our Staff:

The post holder is required to carry out the duties in accordance with the SCI anti-harassment policy.

Counter Fraud

The role holder is required to take all necessary and appropriate steps to prevent fraud, bribery, and corruption within their areas of responsibility, report and respond to all incidents and concerns and comply with the Counter-Fraud, Bribery and Corruption Policy and Procedure. All types of fraud, bribery, and corruption must be prevented, including where it benefits the organisation (SCI).

The Organisation

We employ approximately 25,000 people across the globe and work on the ground in over 100 countries to help children affected by crises, or those that need better healthcare, education and child protection. We also campaign and advocate at the highest levels to realise the right of children and to ensure their voices are heard.

We are working towards three breakthroughs in how the world treats children by 2030:

  • No child dies from preventable causes before their 5th birthday
  • All children learn from a quality basic education and that,
  • Violence against children is no longer tolerated

We know that great people make a great organization, and that our employees play a crucial role in helping us achieve our ambitions for children. We value our people and offer a meaningful and rewarding career, along with a collaborative and inclusive workplace where ambition, creativity, and integrity are highly valued.

Application Information

Please apply using a cover letter and up-to-date CV as a single document. Please also include details of your current remuneration and salary expectations.

We need to keep children safe so our selection process, which includes rigorous background checks, reflects our commitment to the protection of children from abuse.

All employees are expected to carry out their duties in accordance with our global anti-harassment policy.

Save the Children does not charge a fee at any stage of the recruitment process.

Reference Check will be done for all candidates- so the application to include reference details. The selected candidate needs to be ready to join within 24 hours of offer.

Sr. Finance coordinator position having responsibility of finance operation at flood response area. The position will ensure that all financial transactions meet compliance to local statutory law and SC accounting policies.

SCOPE OF ROLE:

Reports to: Field Operation lead

Technical Reporting to : Finance Director

Staff reporting to this post: NA

Role Dimensions:

KEY AREAS OF ACCOUNTABILITY:

Strategic financial information and monitoring:

  • Provide a high standard of financial accounting in emergency programmes, ensuring compliance to local statutory law and SC accounting policies.
  • Ensure accounting systems, policies, internal controls and procedures are quickly established for the collection of accurate, complete and timely financial data (e.g.: budgets, forecasts, expenditure, and delegation of authority).
  • Develop effective relationships with existing Country finance staff
  • Ensure that Save the Children’s commitment to improving quality and accountability in humanitarian work is upheld, through reference to the Sphere Project Humanitarian Charter and Minimum Standards, the NGO Code of Conduct, and other relevant tools.

Internal controls:

  • Support the Response Field Operation Lead and/or Country Finance Director to identify, assess, input, recommend on the existing and desired reconciliation process (reporting assurance mechanism) between
  • Finance, Procurement, Logistics, Distribution, M&E that will ensure accountable reporting to donors on all humanitarian inputs (items delivered to beneficiaries.
  • Take appropriate steps to minimise the risk of fraud or theft.
  • Monitor coding of emergency expenditures and ensure timely adjustments when activation of new awards with relevant audit trail
  • Ensure the security of all cash and assets (e.g.: regular cash and bank reconciliation, fixed asset and inventory physical checks).
  • Support on Cash Transfer programming activities from feasibility assessment to implementation, and ensure accountability by enforcing adequate controls
  • Carry out inductions and staff trainings for finance procedures.

Cost recovery and budgeting

  • Support budget holders/ program staff to produce quality budgeting information while ensuring all relevant stakeholders are involved in the budgeting process.
  • Provide accurate and on time BVAs to awards team to ensure monthly budget monitoring
  • Assist the Country Finance to prepare donor financial reports and proposal budgets.
  • Ensure all donor requirements (financial & reporting) are complied with and that proposals and financial reports are submitted on time.

Cash flow

  • Manage the cash flow to ensure timely and secure transfer of funds to meet programme needs, liaising with local bankers as required and provide the necessary checks and balances to ensure that money is spent effectively, efficiently and in line with donor requirements.
  • Closely monitor the cash management at partner level to ensure effective utilization of fund.
  • Prepare Fund utilization statement of partner each month and send to country office each month while requesting fund to partners.

Partner’s Financial Management:

  • Support to partner NGOs for OPMIS setup and provide required orientation to staff.
  • Support on the preparation of phased budget of project budget with the subaward creation and amendment as per SCI requirements.
  • Maintain excellent relationships with Partners, both in terms of strategic positioning and quality monitoring.
  • Support to ensure partners are clear on their assigned tasks and SC’s zero tolerance policies, and the clauses of agreement signed between SC and partner.
  • Schedule partner visit, review system, and assist in capacity building of partners through coaching / training /orientation/reviewing documents / updating new policies etc.

Other

  • Ensure that audit recommendations are implemented as per donor rules and regulations.
  • Represents and coordinates both internal and external meetings as required.
  • Contribute to effective operation of emergency response.
  • Other tasks will be assigned by supervisor based on need.

Accountability:

  • holds the team and partners accountable to deliver on their responsibilities – giving them the freedom to deliver in the best way they see fit, providing the necessary development to improve performance and applying appropriate consequences when results are not achieved.

  • sets ambitious and challenging goals for themselves and their team, takes responsibility for their own personal development and encourages their team to do the same.
  • widely shares their personal vision for Save the Children, engages and motivates others.
  • future orientated, thinks strategically and on a global scale.

Collaboration:

  • values diversity, sees it as a source of competitive strength.
  • approachable, good listener, easy to talk to.

Creativity:

  • develops and encourages new and innovative solutions.
  • willing to take disciplined risks.

Integrity:

Essential

  • Minimum of 4 years’ (3 years for GSI) of job experience on Financial Management/Partner management/Monitoring/Partner Capacity Building with master’s degree in accounting/ finance/ economics or related field OR minimum of 6 years ( 4 years for GSI group) of experience on Financial Management/Partner management/Monitoring/Partner Capacity Building with bachelor’s degree in accounting/ finance/ economics or related field
  • Knowledge of the requirements and experience managing grants from the major emergency donors including budgeting, eligibility issues, compliance management, and reporting.
  • Experience of coaching and capacity building of staffs
  • Good attention to detail and analytical skills
  • IT literate (i.e. Word, advanced Excel, Outlook, Internet Explorer, financial systems).
  • Cultural awareness and ability to build relationships quickly with a wide variety of people
  • Patient, adaptable, flexible, able to improvise and remain responsive and communicate clearly and effectively under pressure
  • Excellent planning, management and coordination skills, with the ability to organise a demanding workload comprised of diverse and challenging tasks and responsibilities
  • Strong communication (written and spoken), and interpersonal skills in English, with experience in managing multicultural teams
  • Ability and willingness to work under pressure as part of a diverse professional team.
  • Having full commitment to the values and principles of Save the Children

EXPERIENCE AND SKILLS

Desirable

​Position Title: Finance and Administration Officer – Humanitarian Response
​Location: Kathmandu, with frequent visit to the project locations
Reports to: DIDRM Coordinator, with dotted line reporting to the Finance Manager
Application Deadline: Application will remain open until a suitable candidate is identified.
Contract Type: Fixed term
Contract Duration: Till February 2027

​About CBM Global

​CBM Global works alongside people with disabilities in low- and middle-income countries to fight poverty and exclusion and transform lives. Check out our website and LinkedIn profile to learn more. Drawing on over 100 years of experience, we work with the most marginalised in society to:

  • Break the cycle of poverty and disability
  • Treat and prevent conditions that lead to disability; and
  • Build inclusive communities where everyone can enjoy their human rights and achieve their full potential.

We work in over 20 countries, investing in long-term, authentic partnerships with the Disability Movement and multiplying our impact by delivering a combination of inclusive community-based programmes, advocacy for national and global policy change and inclusion advice to other organisations. CBM Global is a worldwide federation with the following Members: CBM Australia, CBM Ireland, CBM Kenya, CBM New Zealand, CBM Switzerland, and CBM UK.

​About the Role

​CBM Global Nepal has initiated a humanitarian response in areas affected by the devastating flash floods in the Bhotekoshi River and downstream river systems. The response covers affected communities in the Rasuwa, Nuwakot, and Dhading districts and focuses on mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS), basic needs assistance, provision of assistive devices, rehabilitation services, and advocacy and technical support to ensure the inclusion of persons with disabilities in the overall humanitarian response.

The Finance and Administration Officer is responsible for overseeing the overall financial and administrative functions of the humanitarian response project, working in close coordination with the Country Office Finance and Administration teams.

​S/he ensures effective financial management of the project by monitoring the utilization of project budgets in line with approved work plans, and CBM Global’s policies and procedures. S/he works closely with partner organizations to provide guidance and support on grant management, financial reporting, and compliance. Additionally, s/he provides administrative and procurement support as needed to ensure the efficient functioning of the country office and successful implementation of the project.

Key Responsibilities

Financial Management

  • Oversee the financial management of the project in close coordination with the project team and partner organizations
  • Establish, implement, and maintain financial procedures and internal controls in line with organisational policies and applicable laws and regulations.
  • Review financial documents, receipts, invoices, and supporting documentation to ensure transactions are accurate, complete, valid, verifiable, and authorized.
  • Monitor financial risks and recommend corrective actions to ensure sound financial management.​

Budget Management

  • Monitor partner budget implementation rates in relation to fund transfers and ensure timely disbursement of project funds to partners.
  • Support periodic budget reviews, revisions, and amendments as required.
  • Prepare monthly forecasts, budget plans, and expenditure reports in collaboration with project teams.
  • Analyze budget variances and provide recommendations to support effective financial decision-making.​

Partner Support

  • Ensure partner staffs are aware and comply with the statutory regulations, CBM policies and guidelines, and partnership agreements.
  • Provide required support to the partners for effective management of project finances, preparation of financial reports and others as required.

Location: Nepal – Kathmandu
Workplace Type: On-site
Hours:40

Job Family: Programme
Division: International
Grade: National D1

Closing Date: 10 September 2026

Salary and benefits: As per national pay scale

Flexible working: We believe flexible working is key to building the Organization of the future, so we’re open to talking through the type of flexible arrangements which might work for you. However, we think this role would work particularly well as a full-time role for 40 hours per week.

The Role

The Emergency Response Team provides timely, effective and accountable emergency assistance to populations affected by disasters and humanitarian crises. The team coordinates with government authorities, partners, communities and humanitarian actors to deliver quality humanitarian programming and strengthen local response capacity. To provide overall field-level leadership, coordination, representation, and oversight of Oxfam’s emergency response interventions in Nuwakot district, ensuring effective implementation by partner organizations and timely coordination with the Response Manager and humanitarian stakeholders. The role will support partners to deliver quality, accountable and gender-responsive humanitarian assistance to flood-affected communities while ensuring compliance with Oxfam standards, donor requirements and humanitarian principles.

Who we’re looking for

We are looking for someone who has the following experience, knowledge and competencies.

Education: Bachelor’s degree in Disaster Management, Development Studies, Social Sciences, Humanitarian Studies or a related field with a minimum of five (5) years of relevant experience, OR a Master’s degree in a related field with a minimum of two (2) years of relevant experience in humanitarian and emergency response programming.

Emergency Response Delivery

Lead and oversee timely, quality, and compliant implementation of emergency response activities, including assessments, planning, monitoring, risk management, and ensuring gender-responsive and accountable programming.

Coordination and Representation

Represent Oxfam in humanitarian coordination forums and maintain effective relationships with government authorities, partners, donors, UN agencies, and other stakeholders to ensure coordinated and effective response delivery.

Partnership Management

Manage and support implementing partners to ensure quality programme delivery, compliance with donor and Oxfam requirements, capacity strengthening, and accountability.

Team Management

Provide leadership and supervision to district response teams, foster collaboration and staff development, and ensure staff wellbeing, safeguarding compliance, and adherence to Oxfam values.

Monitoring, Learning and Reporting

Ensure effective monitoring, reporting, quality assurance, documentation of lessons learned, and regular communication on programme progress, risks, challenges, and opportunities.

What we offer

Oxfam is committed to providing a fair compensation package and to providing a flexible, supportive, working environment.

This role will provide you with an opportunity to make a difference in Oxfam by working closely with a group of passionate people that are specialists in their field of Gender, WASH and Water Governance, Humanitarian and DRM and so forth along with the national and international training and development opportunities. Our offer consists of fair pay and competitive benefits package. At Oxfam, we believe that every aspect of our work can lead to a positive outcome. If you have the same opinion, together with the ability to meet the challenges involved, this role offers scope for immense personal fulfilment – as well as outstanding opportunities to develop your career.

We offer:

We offer a competitive salary and a range of additional benefits to staff including flexible working options, generous pension scheme, annual leave, additional leave allowances, company sick pay, life assurance and a range of other benefits.

From the day you join Oxfam we invite you to stretch and learn in your role. Our wide range of Learning & Development opportunities includes in-house courses, e-learning modules, on-the job learning opportunities, coaching and mentoring, and much more.

You can read more about all Oxfam has to offer here.

Flexfam:

We believe flexible working is key to building the Oxfam of the future, so we’re open to talking through the type of flexible arrangements which might work for you. We think this role would work particularly well as such as part-time, job share, hybrid.

How to apply:
As part of your online application, Please upload an up-to-date CV and a cover letter, clearly explaining your suitability against the essential criteria in the job profile by 10 September 2026.

Please note that only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis, and Oxfam reserves the right to close the recruitment process and make an appointment before the closing date.

Our values and commitment to safeguarding

Oxfam is committed to preventing any type of unwanted behaviour at work including sexual harassment, exploitation and abuse, lack of integrity and financial misconduct; and committed to promoting the welfare of children, young people, adults and beneficiaries with whom Oxfam GB engages. Oxfam expects all staff and volunteers to share this commitment through our code of conduct. We place a high priority on ensuring that only those who share and demonstrate our values are recruited to work for us.

The post holder will undertake the appropriate level of training and is responsible for ensuring that they understand and work within the safeguarding policies of the organisation.

All offers of employment will be subject to satisfactory references and appropriate screening checks, which can include criminal records and terrorism finance checks. Oxfam GB also participates in the Inter Agency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme. In line with this Scheme, we will request information from job applicants’ previous employers about any findings of sexual exploitation, sexual abuse and/or sexual harassment during employment, or incidents under investigation when the applicant left employment. By submitting an application, the job applicant confirms his/her understanding of these recruitment procedures.

We are committed to ensuring diversity and gender equality within our organisation and encourage applicants from diverse backgrounds to apply.

About us

Oxfam is a global community who believe poverty isn’t inevitable. It’s an injustice that can be overcome. We are shop volunteers, women’s right activists, marathon runners, aid workers, coffee farmers, street fundraisers, goat herders, policy experts, campaigners, water engineers and more. And we won’t stop until everyone can live life without poverty for good.

Oxfam GB is a member of international confederation of 21 organisations working together with partners and local communities in the areas of humanitarian, development and campaigning, in more than 90 countries.

A thriving diverse Oxfam:

It’s people power that brings about change. To play our part as a global organisation working to overcome poverty and inequality, we need equality, diversity and inclusion across our community of staff, partners and volunteers. Together, we’re committed to becoming a more diverse workforce, better able to tackle the global challenges that face our world today.

To do that:

  • We need to dismantle the unequal power structures that exist everywhere, this including Oxfam and the wider development and charity sectors.
  • We need an inclusive Oxfam where everyone can bring who they are to our work and feels celebrated for the differences they bring.
  • We want and need everyone, and that means we need you.

Posiiton: Emergency Response Coordinator

Location: Nuwakot, Nepal

Position Status: Full-time, Contract

About Mercy Corps

Mercy Corps is a leading global organization powered by the belief that a better world is possible. In disaster, in hardship, in more than 40 countries around the world, we partner to put bold solutions into action helping people triumph over adversity and build stronger communities from within. Now, and for the future.

The Program Summary

On 26 August 2026, a glacier and rockfall avalanche near the Rasuwagadhi border triggered a catastrophic debris-flow flood along the Bhotekoshi–Trishuli corridor, severely affecting Rasuwa, Nuwakot, and Dhading, districts. Search and rescue operations led by NDRRMA and other responders are ongoing. The disaster has resulted in significant loss of life, injuries, displacement, and extensive damage to infrastructure and livelihoods. Thousands of affected people are facing critical shortages of shelter, water, food, and sanitation supplies. Mercy Corps Nepal is responding to the disaster supporting the affected families with immediate relief and enabling recovery.

The Position

The Response Coordinator will offer technical assistance to the project, supporting the emergency response for the flooding in Rauswa, Nuwakot and Dhading. The coordinator will work under the direct supervision of the Country Director and will collaborate closely with the implementing and technical partners, as well as the Financial Service Provider. The coordinator will also establish strong relationships with humanitarian actors, agencies active in the targeted municipality and districts, and government officials to ensure the quality of project interventions, focusing mainly on the timely completion of activities within the given timeframe, avoiding sporadic distribution of support, and providing comprehensive support to selected households to meet multiple needs.

Essential Responsibilities

The specific duties and responsibilities of the Emergency Response Coordinator include, but are not limited to, the following:

  • Lead the implementation of humanitarian response activities in accordance with the project plans, budgets, and timelines.
  • Ensure effective coordination and close engagement with stakeholders to lead project implementation, including endorsing vulnerability criteria and selecting beneficiaries.
  • Support execution of agreements with partner/s and Technical and Financial Service Providers (T/FSP) for project interventions.
  • Work with partners to undertake rapid market assessments to deploy sectoral CVA assistance, identify appropriate modalities for cash and voucher assistance, and produce reports.
  • Ensure project interventions adhere to quality standards, humanitarian principles, and organizational policies.
  • Extend technical support to partners through the MCN finance unit on financial and procurement procedures for CVA, disbursement mechanisms, and mobilization.
  • Support mobilization of T/FSPs for the deployment of digital CVA modalities.
  • Support orientation for vendors and enumerators, register flood-affected targeted households, and generate reports through TSP.
  • Facilitate the redemption of CVA assistance through electronic vouchers and cash transfers, working alongside T/FSPs.
  • Assist in undertaking Post-Distribution Monitoring (PDM) within two to four weeks of support through call centers.
  • Lead issue logs and ensure the project accountability matrix is duly established for accurate targeting and CVA programming.
  • Manage partner relations, facilitating regular coordination meetings to review progress, address challenges, and ensure timely implementation.
  • Participate in technical meetings with local authorities, clusters, NGOs, and relevant institutions.
  • Work closely with the Country CARM focal person to ensure participants, communities, and stakeholders are oriented on CARM and safeguarding, and that issues are managed per MC policy.
  • Prepare the project work plan and detailed implementation plan.
  • Track budget expenditure and prepare weekly, monthly, and final reports.
  • Lead the learning process of documentation and capture case stories from the field.

Safeguarding Responsbilities

  • Actively learns about safeguarding and integrates it into their work, including safeguarding risks and mitigations related to their area of work.
  • Practices the values of Mercy Corps including respecting the dignity and well-being of participants and fellow team members.
  • Encourages openness and communication in their team; encourages team members to submit reports if they have any concerns using reporting mechanisms e.g., Integrity Hotline and other options.

Supervisory Responsibility

  • Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning Officer

Accountability

  • Reports Directly To: Country Director
  • Works Directly With: Program Quality and Partnership Manager, Country CARM Focal point, and project technical partner team members as required.

Accountability to Participants and Stakeholders

Mercy Corps team members are expected to support all efforts toward accountability, specifically to our program participants, community partners, other stakeholders, and to international standards guiding international relief and development work. We are committed to actively engaging communities as equal partners in the design, monitoring and evaluation of our field projects.

Minimum Qualification & Transferable Skills

  • Bachelor’s degree in development studies, environmental science, Social Science, or any other relevant fields. Master’s Degree preferred
  • At least 5 years’ experience of humanitarian/emergency response, recovery and inclusion especially in implementation with a strong background on coordination with multiple stakeholders and humanitarian program management for government, national or international non-government agencies.
  • Experience working in cash transfer modalities including both cash and vouchers, with specific experience and/or knowledge of digital cash transfer options.
  • Experiences working in partnerships; coordination among different stakeholders and organizations at local and provincial levels is required.
  • Good understanding of humanitarian contexts, humanitarian coordination system, humanitarian standard and principles and humanitarian accountability initiatives in Nepal.
  • Demonstrated ability to work in complex environments under tight deadlines.
  • Strong partnership management skills, including capacity to coordinate with teams remotely.
  • Excellent spoken and written English and Nepali language skills and ability to interact effectively with international and national staff.

Success Factors

A successful candidate will have the ability to live and work closely with a diverse team of individuals in a highly intense and fluid work and security environment with a capacity to spark innovative approaches to programming and inspire groups to collaborate closely to implement high-quality humanitarian programs. S/he will have proven ability to learn quickly, take initiative, and be accountable for results, with an ability and willingness to remain mobile for short-term and/or long-term as necessary within the region, based on programmatic needs. An ability to work independently and as part of a team, with curiosity about and sensitivity to new cultures, a desire and ability to learn and grow, both personally and professionally, and a great sense of humor.

The most successful Mercy Corps team members have a strong commitment to teamwork and accountability, thrive in evolving and changing environments and make effective written and verbal communication a priority in all situations. Mercy Corps Team members represent the agency both during and outside of work hours when deployed in a field posting or on a visit/short-term assignment to a field posting. Team members are expected to conduct themselves in a professional manner and respect local laws, customs and MC’s policies, procedures, and values at all times and in all in-country venues.

Ongoing Learning

In support of our belief that learning organizations are more effective, efficient and relevant to the communities we serve, we empower all team members to dedicate 5% of their time to learning activities that further their personal and/or professional growth and development.

Team Engagement and Effectiveness

Achieving our mission starts with how we build our team and collaborate. By bringing together individuals with a variety of experiences, backgrounds, and perspectives, we strengthen our ability to solve complex challenges and drive innovation. We foster a culture of trust and respect, where every team member is valued for their contributions, empowered to reach their full potential, and motivated to do their best work.

We recognize that building a strong and effective team is an ongoing process, and we remain committed to learning, improving, and growing together.

Equal Employment Opportunity

Mercy Corps is an equal opportunity employer committed to providing equal employment opportunities to all employees and qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, color, sex, sexual orientation, religion or belief, national origin, age, disability, marital status, veteran status, or any other characteristics protected under applicable law.

Safeguarding & Ethics

Mercy Corps is committed to ensuring that all individuals we come into contact with through our work, whether team members, community members, program participants or others, are treated with respect and dignity. We are committed to the core principles regarding prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse laid out by the UN Secretary General and IASC and have signed on to the The Misconduct Disclosure Scheme. We will not tolerate child abuse, sexual exploitation, abuse, or harassment by or of our team members. As part of our commitment to a safe and inclusive work environment, team members are expected to conduct themselves in a professional manner, respect local laws and customs, and to adhere to Mercy Corps Code of Conduct Policies and values at all times. Team members are required to complete mandatory Code of Conduct elearning courses upon hire and on an annual basis.

As an applicant, if you witness or experience any form of sexual misconduct during the recruitment process, please report this to Mercy Corps Integrity Hotline (integrityhotline@mercycorps.org).
