Reintegration and Economic Mobility through Inclusive Public Employment Services (ReMi) Project, Phase II (subject to the approval of the ReMi Phase II) is a bilateral initiative between the Governments of Nepal and Switzerland. It is implemented by the Ministry of Youth, Labour and Employment (MoYLE), respective provincial line ministries and participating local governments. The project is funded by the Swiss Agency for Development and Cooperation (SDC) and Helvetas Nepal provides technical assistance.

Helvetas Nepal invites applications from dynamic and committed Nepali citizens for the following positions (subject to the approval of the ReMi Phase II):

Employment and Reintegration Services Coordinator – 1 position(s) – Open For All

Duty Station: Ministry of Youth, Labour and Employment (MoYLE), Singha durbar, Kathmandu

Job Description

Job purpose: The primary purpose of this position is to work closely with MoYLE to support policy, guidelines and procedures that enhance efficient and effective public employment services delivery at Employment, Skills and Entrepreneurship Centers (ESECs) in Nepal, including support for reintegration of returnee migrants. The role aims to strengthen the ESECs across Nepal to ensure its full function and provide holistic and quality services on public employment services, including labour, employment, migration and reintegration. Additionally, it involves contributing to the promotion of productive domestic and foreign employment opportunities while fostering synergies with relevant development partners.

Roles and Responsibilities

Specific roles and responsibilities of this position include, but are not limited to the following:

1. Coordination, Collaboration and Networking

  • Support MoYLE to organise the thematic committee meeting on labour and employment, public employment services, and digitalization; follow up on the decisions of the committee and ensure that the key related agenda are discussed in the meeting.
  • Enhance inter-ministry coordination and coordinate with government and stakeholders at all levels to strengthen policies, procedures, and guidelines, particularly related to public employment services (including migration and reintegration) and digitalization.
  • Effective coordination and facilitation among various departments, projects (ReMi, SaMi, K-HaMi and other relevant projects), and development partners (SDC, World Bank, ILO, FCDO, KOICA, JICA, ADB) within MoYLE, as well as across provincial and local governments and local-level associations.
  • Enhance program complementarity and strategic coherence with all relevant projects through aligned government strategies, policies, guidelines, communication on public employment services, labour migration and reintegration services.
  • Facilitate aligned support from relevant projects and development partners to MoYLE and the ESECs to improve governance, operations, and financing frameworks of the ESECs.
  • Engage with the Foreign Employment Board, Department of Foreign Employment, and others in planning, monitoring and implementation of integrated public employment services, integration of digital systems and implementation of respective reintegration programs, ensuring that ReMi interventions are aligned and coordinated with all other related programs and projects.
  • Coordinate with all levels of government to establish one door ESEC and digitalization.

2. Technical assistance

  • Review any available research, labour market analyses, the employment services assessments, etc to inform and facilitate policy and programmatic discussion within the Ministry, projects and with development partners.
  • Draw learning and experiences of ReMi project and support MoYLE to incorporate the learning in reintegration, public employment service and private sector related policies, guidelines and programs.
  • Be updated on various inter-governmental regional consultative processes and inform/sensitize senior government officials about the importance of and engagement in such platforms.

3. Institutional and Operational Mechanism to Strengthen ESECs

  • Support MoYLE for coordination and consultation with different divisions, sections and institutions providing reintegration and public employment service to review the service packages of ESECs and support to enhance and clarify the role and responsibilities of ESECs.
  • Support MoYLE to develop and implement capacity building strategy for updated labour, employment, migration, reintegration and public employment services provided through the ESECs including scope of work, resources (human, technical and financial) required, implementation of standard operating procedures, and monitoring and quality assurance frameworks.
  • Support MoYLE in developing and implementing the digitalisation plan related to labour, employment, migration and reintegration in close coordination with digitalization specialist.
  • Identify opportunities for systematic engagement with private sector, the formalization of linkages and referrals with relevant public and private sectors, and the employers’ associations, cooperatives, and other relevant member-based organizations.

4. Coordination support for ReMi Project

  • Work as a facilitator between ReMi project and the MoYLE in coordination with Deputy Team Leader and other ReMi team members.
  • Facilitate communication and collaboration between ReMi PSU team and concerned Ministries/Departments at federal level as required.
  • Facilitate and support MoYLE on planning and budgeting in relation to the project mandate.
  • Extend support on public finance management including planning and reporting.
  • Support the ReMi team by providing policy-related information, facilitation, and timely updates on policy changes and processes at MoYLE and other relevant ministries concerning labor, employment, migration, and reintegration.
  • Support to organize steering/advisory committee meetings and other meetings with MoYLE.

5. Compliance to policies, rules/regulations, and guidelines

  • Adhere to relevant policies, procedures, regulations and guidelines of HELVETAS Swiss Intercooperation (Code of Conduct; NPR-Nepal; Finance Manual; Security Response Guide; Gender Equality and Social Inclusion Guide; Mobbing, Sexual Harassment & Abuse of Authority; Code of Conduct Against Corruption etc.) and other specific policies applicable for ReMi.
  • Ensure Conflict Sensitive Program Management at all levels.
  • Ensure compliance of all the terms and conditions agreed between HELVETAS Swiss Intercooperation Nepal and the donor.

6. Other Specific Responsibilities

  • Professionally discharge other mutually agreed tasks assigned by the ReMi Deputy Team Leader.

Job Requirements:

  • A. Minimum Education Attainment: Master’s degree in Social Sciences, Economics, Development Cooperation or in any relevant discipline.
  • B. Minimum Professional Experience: Minimum 5 years of working experience in project/ programme with at least 3 years dedicated experience in governance, public policy development, employment services and private sector engagement. Having experience in labour migration and working with government system is an added value. Commitment towards gender equality, social inclusion and poverty reduction; and sensitivity towards migrant workers and their families.

C. Required Competencies:

  • Ability of working in a complex multi-stakeholder project with public institution and systems building objectives.
  • Sound understanding on migration, reintegration and social protection are an added value.
  • Knowledge on project cycle management, including outcome/results-based project implementation, monitoring and reporting.
  • Strong social skills for collaboration with wide variety of stakeholders including three levels of government agencies, national and international development partners, private sector and civil society.
  • Strong understanding on governance system, particularly on the federal context of Nepal.
  • Strong networking skills, ability to link various actors and institutions.
  • Strong communication, negotiation and facilitating skills.
  • Excellent analytical, conceptual and programmatic competencies.
  • Excellent reporting and writing skills.
  • Strong motivator, a team player, and collaborator. .
  • Commitment towards gender equality, social inclusion, and poverty reduction.
  • Fluency in English and Nepali, both written and orally is essential.
  • Knowledge on digitalization will be an added value.
  • IT: Proficiency in using office application software.

Additional Information

Duration: Initially for 3 years

Salary and Benefits: As per the rules and regulation of Helvetas Nepal.

Application Procedures: Interested candidates who meet above requirements are requested to visit our website at http://apply.helvetasnepal.org and submit application through online portal. Detail job description is available on the website.

Any telephone inquiries and/or attempts to apply undue influence will result disqualification of candidates. Only short-listed candidates will be contacted for the selection process. Helvetas Nepal reserves the right to reject any or all applications without assigning any reasons.

Helvetas Nepal promotes workforce diversity and applies positive discrimination to candidates from discriminated groups (Women, Dalit, Janajati, Madhesi/Terai, and other minority communities).

The trainee will learn about the different phases of migration, as well as the related challenges and prospects. Under the overall guidance and supervision of the Provincial Program Manager, the trainee will have the opportunity to learn about the dynamics of the labour migration sector, project/program cycle management, the Migration Resource Centres (MRCs), Employment Skills and Entrepreneurship Centres (ESEC), federal state building and the role of the three spheres of government and their linkages to the migration sector.

Learning areas

1. Project management and implementation

  • Participate in workshops, dialogues, and trainings on migration/reintegration and foreign employment;
  • Support on program monitoring, review, and reporting;
  • Engage/support to program-related research and evaluation;
  • Support to enhance the program quality of the Migration Resource Center;
  • Support in organizing consultations, workshops, etc., drafting letters and minutes;
  • Support in the development of Information, Education, and Communication (IEC) materials and social media content;
  • Understand the employment and migration governance-related issues and contribute to the SaMi program; and
  • Learn and follow the Conflict-Sensitive Programme Management at all levels.

2. Federal state-building, planning, and budgeting

  • Support in data management of program components, including migration/ reintegration profile and safer migration/ reintegration guidelines;
  • Provide support in organizing consultation meetings, inter-government coordination meetings, and workshops, etc., and drafting letters and minutes;
  • Understand the role of different governments (Federal, Provincial, and Local) on employment and migration governance and associated issues, and contribute to the SaMi program;
  • Engage and learn by participating in programs on migration related services organized by Local Governments, and
  • Support the program team in coordination with the relevant stakeholders as required.

3. Data Management and Reporting

  • Understand and support data management, data collection, and document best practices;
  • Learn and support in documenting case studies, best practices, program photos, and videos under the program;
  • Support in monitoring of project components based on the monitoring checklist.

4. Others

  • Act proactively in performing the aforesaid tasks;
  • Provide support in other tasks as required and requested; and
  • Have a learning attitude and expand your knowledge and experience in safer migration ecosystems.

5. Compliance with policies, rules/regulations, and guidelines

  • Adhere to relevant policies, procedures, regulations, and guidelines of HELVETAS Swiss Intercooperation (Personnel, Financial, Administrative policies; Security Response Guide; Gender Equality and Social
  • Inclusion Guide; Sexual Harassment & Mobbing Policy; Code of Conduct Against Corruption, etc.) and other specific policies applicable; and
    Compliance with the GoN and SDC policies and approaches as relevant and required.

Eligibility Criteria and Competencies

A. Eligibility Criteria:

  • Bachelor’s degree in the field of social science, humanities, public administration, education, law, health, or any other relevant field.
  • Fresh graduate with no prior job experience. Completion of a bachelor’s degree within two years while applying for the position.
  • Willingness to undertake extensive field travel within and outside the province.
  • Commitment towards gender equality, social inclusion, poverty reduction, and sensitivity towards migrant workers and their families.
  • Proactive and a keen learning attitude and a sense of responsibility.
  • Woman/man from Dalit, Janajati, Madhesi/Terai caste/ethnicity, ethnic and religious minorities, discriminated Newar castes.

B. Competencies Required:

  • Knowledge of labor migration and reintegration of Nepali migrant workers.
  • Willingness and interest in travel to project field locations (70%) within the provinces, and other provinces as well.
  • Eagerness and self-initiation to learn and develop a career in the migration sector.
  • Basic understanding of the functioning of local government and federalism principles and the political context.
  • Reliable, sincere, and having a positive attitude.
  • Excellent time management, task prioritization skills, and result orientation.
  • Polite with good interpersonal and intercultural competencies.
  • Good English & Nepali skills (oral, written, and typing); knowledge of local languages is an advantage.
  • Good facilitation and communication skills, including the ability to represent and interact effectively with different stakeholders.
  • Good team player and effective communicator.

Additional Information

Duration: 1 year (12 months) with a fixed duration.

Stipend and benefits: As per the rules and regulations of Helvetas Nepal.

Local candidates from remote municipalities of the respective province will have an advantage.

Interested and committed fresh graduates are requested to visit our website at https://apply.helvetasnepal.org and submit their application through the online portal. Detailed learning objectives are available on the website.

Any telephone enquiries/and or attempts to apply undue influence will result in the disqualification of candidates. Only short-listed candidates will be contacted for the selection process. Helvetas Nepal reserves the right to reject any or all applications without assigning any reasons.

Helvetas Nepal promotes workforce diversity and applies positive discrimination to candidates from discriminated groups. The traineeship opportunity is focused only for woman/ man from Dalit, woman from Janjati, Madhesi/Terai caste/ethnicity, ethnic and religious minorities, discriminated Newar castes.

Group of Helping Hands (SAHAS) Nepal is a non-profit, non-governmental organization established in 1996. Since its establishment, SAHAS Nepal has been working with vulnerable and socially excluded communities through social mobilization, grassroots organization building, Community-Based Network Organization (CBNO) formation and capacity development. SAHAS Nepal implements diverse programmes and projects in sustainable agriculture and food security, climate change, education, and related areas across 21 districts of Nepal.

SAHAS Nepal will implement a scholarship project titled “Bridging Futures: Education Access Initiative.” The project aims to support academically qualified young people and civil society actors from disadvantaged and marginalized groups to access higher education, develop their leadership capacities, and contribute to socio-ecological change and sustainable development in their communities and Nepal.

SAHAS Nepal invites applications from energetic, committed, competent, and creative Nepali citizens for the following positions.

Posiiton: Scholarship Coordinator

Required Number: 1

Duty Station: Kathmandu, with approximately 60% travel to project locations

Academic Qualification and Experience

  • Master’s degree in Education, Social Science, Development Studies, Management, or another relevant discipline.
  • Minimum 3 years of relevant professional experience, preferably in education, scholarship management, youth development, social inclusion, or development projects.
  • Demonstrated experience in project planning, implementation, monitoring, budgeting, reporting, and team coordination.
  • Good understanding of Nepal’s higher education system, education policies, scholarship mechanisms, and relevant government regulations.
  • Strong networking and coordination skills with universities, colleges, government agencies, development partners, and other education stakeholders.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication, facilitation, negotiation, and interpersonal skills in both Nepali and English.
  • Strong leadership and team management skills, with the ability to motivate team members and work effectively with diverse stakeholders.
  • Strong computer skills, including MS Office applications; knowledge of project management and reporting systems will be an advantage.
  • Willingness and ability to travel frequently to project locations.

Key Responsibilities

Project Leadership and Implementation

  • Lead overall implementation of the scholarship project in accordance with project objectives, approved plans, policies, and donor requirements.
  • Develop and regularly update annual, quarterly, and monthly implementation plans.
  • Provide technical and managerial guidance to project team members.

Scholarship Management

  • Lead and oversee the scholarship application, screening, selection, award, and renewal processes in a transparent, inclusive, and accountable manner.
  • Ensure that scholarship implementation complies with approved criteria, project guidelines, and applicable policies.
  • Maintain regular communication with scholars and ensure they understand programme rules, responsibilities, academic requirements, and reporting obligations.

Coordination and Networking

  • Establish and maintain effective coordination with universities, colleges, academic institutions, finance departments, teachers, government authorities, and other relevant stakeholders.
  • Liaise with universities and colleges to verify student enrolment, academic progress, fee requirements, and other relevant information.
  • Explore opportunities for institutional collaboration and resource sharing to maximize benefits for scholars.

Financial and Administrative Management

  • Monitor project expenditure against approved budgets and ensure compliance with SAHAS Nepal and donor financial requirements.
  • Contribute to budget revisions, financial forecasting, and preparation of financial and narrative reports.

Monitoring, Reporting and Learning

  • Track project progress against agreed targets and indicators.
  • Conduct regular field visits to monitor programme effectiveness and identify challenges and areas for improvement.
  • Prepare timely project reports documenting project achievements, good practices, lessons learned, success stories, and challenges.

Posiiton: Admin and Finance Officer

Required Number: 1

Duty Station: Kathmandu, with approximately 40% travel outside the Kathmandu Valley

Academic Qualification and Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Business Administration, Management, or a related field.
  • Minimum 2 years of relevant professional experience, preferably with NGOs/INGOs, development projects scholarship management.
  • Good knowledge of financial accounting, budgeting, procurement, and administrative systems.
  • Strong working knowledge of MS Excel and other MS Office applications.
  • Experience with Money-Works or similar accounting software will be an advantage.
  • Knowledge of donor financial requirements, taxation, Social Security Fund (SSF), audit procedures, and NGO financial compliance will be an advantage.
  • Good organizational, communication, documentation, and record-keeping skills.
  • Willingness to travel outside the Kathmandu Valley is required.

Key Responsibilities

Financial Management

  • Process and maintain accurate records of tuition payments, scholarships, stipends, allowances, and other payments to scholars and institutions.
  • Maintain proper financial documentation and supporting documents for all project transactions.
  • Monitor project expenditure against approved budgets and provide regular budget updates.
  • Assist in preparing financial reports in accordance with SAHAS Nepal and funding partner requirements.
  • Ensure compliance with organizational financial policies, donor requirements, applicable tax regulations, and audit requirements.

Administration and Procurement

  • Manage procurement of project supplies, equipment, and services in accordance with organizational procedures.
  • Support Scholarship Coordinator in managing logistics during the events and training programs.
  • Maintain organized physical and digital administrative filing systems.
  • Maintain project asset and stock records and ensure proper safeguarding and utilization of project assets.

Human Resource and Compliance Support

  • Support timely processing of staff salaries and benefits.
  • Assist with internal and external audits by maintaining complete and accessible financial and administrative documentation.

Posiiton: Student Support and Scholarship Outreach Facilitator

Required Number: 1

Duty Station: Field

Academic Qualification and Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree in Education, Social Science, Development Studies, Counselling, or another relevant discipline.
  • Minimum 1 year of relevant professional experience, preferably in education, youth development, scholarship programmes, counselling, or social development.
  • Experience in academic counselling, mentoring, youth engagement, community outreach, or student support will be an advantage.
  • Good understanding of Nepal’s education system, higher education opportunities, and relevant policies.
  • Ability to work with students and young people from diverse and disadvantaged backgrounds.
  • Good computer and documentation skills in both Nepali and English.
  • Willingness to travel to schools, communities, colleges, and other project locations.
  • Strong communication, interpersonal, facilitation, mentoring, and networking skills.

Key Responsibilities

Student Support and Mentorship

  • Provide scholars with academic advising, career guidance, mentorship, and regular well-being check-ins.
  • Monitor scholars’ academic progress and identify students who may require additional support.
  • Act as the first point of support when a scholar faces academic, personal, financial, or other challenges that may affect their participation or scholarship eligibility.
  • Maintain appropriate and confidential records of student support and follow-up.

Scholarship Outreach and Recruitment

  • Visit schools, colleges, universities, communities, and other relevant locations to identify and reach potential applicants.
  • Support dissemination of scholarship calls, eligibility criteria, application procedures, and deadlines.

Capacity Building and Networking

  • Develop and maintain networks with schools, colleges, universities, youth groups, community organizations, and other relevant stakeholders.
  • Encourage scholars to participate in learning, leadership, community engagement, and professional development opportunities.

Monitoring and Documentation

  • Maintain updated records of scholar participation, academic progress, support provided, and follow-up actions.
  • Contribute to project monitoring, success stories, case studies, and periodic reports.
  • Provide regular feedback to the Scholarship Coordinator on student needs, emerging challenges, and opportunities for improvement.

Salary and Benefits

Salary and benefits will be provided as per the rules and regulations of SAHAS Nepal and based on the qualifications and experience of the selected candidate.

Application Procedure

Interested Nepali citizens are requested to submit the following documents:

1. An updated Curriculum Vitae (CV).
2. A cover letter clearly indicating the position applied for and demonstrating the candidate’s interest and suitability for the position.
3. Mailing address and telephone number.
4. Details of two professional references, including their contact information.

Applications should be submitted to the Executive Director, SAHAS Nepal, by 10th September 2026, via email at: sahasnepalvacancy@gmail.com

Telephone enquiries will not be entertained. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted for further screening and selection processes.

SAHAS Nepal reserves the right to reject any or all applications without assigning any reason.

Equal Opportunity, Diversity and Inclusion: SAHAS Nepal promotes workforce diversity and inclusion and applies positive discrimination in favour of candidates from marginalized and disadvantaged groups. Applications from women and members of Indigenous, marginalized, and disadvantaged communities are highly encouraged.

Safeguarding and Zero Tolerance: SAHAS Nepal is committed to safeguarding and maintains a zero-tolerance policy toward abuse, exploitation, corruption, bribery, fraud, sexual harassment, and all forms of misconduct.

Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

Posiiton: Compliance Manager
Location: Kathmandu

Jhpiego is an international, non-profit health organization affiliated with The Johns Hopkins University. For 50 years and in over 155 countries, Jhpiego has worked to prevent the needless deaths of women and their families.

Reporting to the Country Director, the Compliance Manager is accountable for identifying risks that hinder the achievement of Jhpiego’s strategic and program objectives, developing standardized approaches to a reduced risk profile in the country office, and leading communications on all fraud-related issues.  Additionally, this position will participate in the annual risk assessment process in partnership with the country teams to develop strategies and action plans that strengthen Jhpiego’s internal controls and compliance capacity.  Other responsibilities include providing guidance, training, and compliance oversight in the areas of procurement, subrecipient monitoring, financial management, and other operational areas as needed.  The Compliance Manager demonstrates excellent organizational and technical skills and is a dedicated, hardworking, and highly motivated professional. S/he should be an effective team player with an innovative and solution-oriented approach, and is capable of managing multiple priorities and delivering results effectively in high-pressure environments. Duty station being in Dhaka or Kathmandu, the Compliance Manager will oversee compliance functions for Jhpiego Bangladesh and Nepal offices.

Working with the Sr. Compliance Director, Jhpiego’s Bangladesh and Nepal office Leadership/ teams, the Compliance Manager ensures program compliance with applicable policies, guidelines, regulations and procedures.

Location: Asia, with preference for Bangladesh & Nepal

Responsibilities

  • Work with the Country Director(s), Director Compliance, Director Finance, country leadership, and HQ teams to establish, maintain, and strengthen effective internal controls, compliance processes, and risk management systems.
  • Develop and implement an annual compliance monitoring and review plan based on the country office project portfolio, including routine monthly and quarterly reviews, spot checks, field visits, and other compliance activities.
  • Monitor compliance with donor regulations, contractual obligations, organizational policies and procedures, and applicable U.S. , host country, and other relevant laws and regulations.
  • Identify areas of compliance vulnerability and risk; conduct risk assessments and support the development, implementation, and monitoring of corrective action plans.
  • Coordinate the organization’s risk management framework and actively work with management to identify, assess, mitigate, and monitor operational, financial, compliance, and programmatic risks.
  • Develop, implement, and maintain effective subrecipient monitoring and oversight systems in accordance with JHU and Jhpiego policies, including monitoring visits, compliance audits, and follow-up on corrective actions.
  • Work with the Finance Director (s) to support external audits, donor reviews, Johns Hopkins University (JHU) audits, and other compliance assessments, and support management in responding to audit findings and implementing recommendations.
  • Track, monitor, and regularly report on the implementation status of audit findings, compliance recommendations, and management action plans to senior leadership.
  • Support the Finance team in review process and other internal control assessments as needed.
  • Prepare and present compliance review reports, risk assessments, and management updates to senior leadership.
  • Develop, deliver, and coordinate compliance and ethics training programs; assess staff training needs and promote awareness of applicable policies, procedures, and regulatory requirements.
  • Provide tools, and guidance to staff and support their implementation across the organization.
  • Maintain and promote an effective compliance and ethics program, including serving as a confidential point of contact for reporting compliance concerns, misconduct, or irregularities.
  • Conduct compliance investigations, special reviews, analytical assignments, and other projects as requested by management.
  • Immediately escalate suspected fraud, gross misconduct, or other significant compliance concerns in accordance with organizational reporting requirements.
  • Collaborate with the global compliance team to review and improve policies, procedures, monitoring tools, templates, and best practices.
  • Participate in Internal Compliance Reviews (ICRs), regional compliance initiatives, and other compliance-related assignments as required.
  • Maintain current knowledge of relevant donor requirements, regulatory developments, compliance standards, and industry best practices.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, Business Administration, or a related field.
  • Postgraduate qualification in a business-related field is an added advantage.
  • Professional certification such as ACCA, CIA, CISA, CPA, or equivalent, with membership in a relevant professional body preferred.
  • Minimum 7-8 years of progressively responsible experience in audit, accounting, compliance, risk management, or internal controls, preferably within an international NGO environment, including at least 2 years in a supervisory or management role.
  • Strong knowledge of accounting principles, auditing standards, internal controls, risk management practices, and compliance frameworks.
  • Demonstrated understanding of donor regulations and compliance requirements, particularly those of the S. Government, Gates Foundation, and other major institutional donors.
  • Good understanding of internal audit methodologies, emerging trends, and international best practices.
  • Proven ability to review, analyze, and interpret financial records, reports, and statements.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications and computer-assisted audit techniques.
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, and decision-making skills, with the ability to exercise sound judgment and manage competing priorities under tight deadlines.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to engage effectively with stakeholders at all levels, both within and outside the organization.
  • Strong interpersonal and people management skills, with the ability to work effectively in multicultural and multidisciplinary environments.
  • Previous experience working with a nonprofit or international development organization is an added advantage.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Ability to read, analyze, and interpret common reports, and agreement documents.
  • Ability to work with mathematical concepts as they relate to auditing and fiscal analysis to include accounting and the budget.
  • Reasoning Ability – ability to define problems, collect data, establish facts, and draw valid conclusions.
  • Ability to manage several major activities simultaneously.
  • Ability to travel independently in new environments.
  • Sensitive to socio-cultural differences in the region
  • Computer literacy, particularly in the use of MS word, Excel and PowerPoint
  • Proficiency in both written and spoken English. Computers skills including use of spreadsheets and/or accounting packages.
  • Knowledge of Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP).
  • Knowledge of internal controls

Position: Humanitarian Response Officer

Required Number: 1 position

Duty Station: Dhading with frequent travel to Nuwakot

Duration: 4 months with possibility of extension based on response needs, performance, and availability of funding.

In response to recent flash flood in Rasuwa, across Nuwakot, Dhading, and Chitwan, DCA Nepal is supporting the government in relief distribution for affected communities, providing emergency relief to families who have lost their homes and belongings. As an initial response, we are distributing essential items to the affected community particularly at Dhading and Nuwakot in coordination with our local partner, as well as all relevant local authorities and other humanitarian organisations.

In this context, DCA is seeking to recruit Humanitarian Response Officer, who will be responsible to coordinate the efforts of humanitarian response works at Dhading and Nuwakot District. S/he will support the planning, implementation, monitoring and coordination work with the district and Palika level offices working closely with partners, and other relevant stakeholders. S/he will be responsible for day-to-day operational coordination and implementation of the response activity, including needs assessments, community and beneficiary identification, activity planning, field implementation, distribution, feedback and monitoring, coordination with local authorities and humanitarian actors maintaining strong data management and operational reporting.

This is a field-oriented position based at Dhading but regular visit to Nuwakot. Under the supervision of DCA Program Manager with agreed plans and delegated authority, s/he is expected to escalate strategic, safeguarding, donor and budget decisions to Crisis Management Team. S/he works closely with the Crisis Management Team to ensure that assistance is delivered rapidly, appropriately and transparently, in accordance with DCA procedures, humanitarian principles and donor requirements.

Roles and Responsibilities:

  • Coordinate and facilitate DCA humanitarian response activities at the district and palika level, including planning, distribution, implementation, monitoring, follow-up, and coordination of response interventions targeting affected and vulnerable populations.
  • Coordinate with local government, partners, other stakeholders and DCA teams to ensure continuity and timely delivery of relief items, cash assistance, and early recovery activities
  • Constant communication and coordination with Focal Persons of DPNet deployed at Nuwakot for related information-management support.
  • Support government bodies in the districts and palikas to manage program and emergency response data by coordinating data collection from the community and identifying beneficiaries ensuring data quality and accuracy, maintaining databases and records, and preparing regular summaries and reports
  • Maintain regular communication with affected communities, ensuring transparent beneficiary verification and support accessible feedback and complaints mechanisms and promptly escalate serious or unresolved concerns.
  • Collect and provide required information to DCA team related to relief distribution, or planning in order to report and complete respective cluster activity reporting in addition to the existing SWC obligation
  • Monitor and document response activities and emerging needs, identify implementation gaps, and provide timely updates and recommendations to the DCA team to support effective decision-making and adaptive response.
  • Provide coordination and technical support to government authorities within the scope of work, including participation in coordination meetings, information sharing, joint planning, and other response-related activities as required.
  • Support DCA team in joint needs assessment- together with other NGOs, in partnership with DPNet – to guide the early recovery and future interventions.
  • Participate in clusters, sector meetings, working groups, joint assessments or other humanitarian coordination mechanisms at district level when requested or delegated
  • Represent DCA professionally at district level when specifically delegated, while referring safeguarding, high-level institutional and donor matters to Crisis Management Team
  • Maintain accurate records of relief distribution, beneficiary registries, and partner activity for accountability and reporting purposes
  • Support partners in implementing accountability mechanisms (feedback/complaints, community consultation) in line with CHS commitments
  • Contribute to concept note and proposal development for emergency and early recovery funding
  • Ensure protection, gender, and inclusion considerations are integrated into response activities, prioritizing vulnerable groups (women, children, elderly, PWD)
  • Other related tasks as assigned by the line manager

Required Qualifications and Experience:

  • Master’s degree in development studies, Rural Development, Social Science, Disaster risk management and Natural Resource Management with 3 years of work experience with an I/NGO or development organization. Preference will be given to Disaster Risk Management.
  • Demonstrated experience in emergencies, working with local government structures (DDMC/DAO), clusters, and INGO/NGO coordination mechanisms
  • Prior experience in cash-based programming, NFI/shelter distribution, or early recovery activities is an advantage
  • Proven experience in data management, analysis, documentation, and reporting.
  • Good interpersonal, active listening, and communication skills, with cultural sensitivity, professionalism, and the ability to remain calm under pressure.
  • Ability to work effectively in challenging field conditions and flexible working hours, while maintaining personal resilience and well-being.
  • Willingness and ability to travel to and stay in disaster-affected and remote areas as required.

Applications consisting of the below will only be considered:

  • CV (max 3 pages)

Please click on APPLY button at the end of this vacancy announcement to apply.

Only short-listed candidates will be contacted.

Closing date for application will be Thursday, 10 September 2026. Only short-listed candidates will be further contacted. This recruitment will be held on a rolling basis and DCA Nepal reserves the right to select a candidate prior to the application closing date.

DCA is committed to ensuring diversity, inclusion and gender equality within our organisation and encourage applicants from diverse backgrounds to apply.

All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, race, religion, sexual orientation, abilities or ethnic affiliation are encouraged to apply for the vacancy. DCA conducts an anti-terror check as part of the recruitment process. It is a prerequisite that you can pass this check and maintain this status throughout your employment with us.

DCA PSEAH Policy is one of zero tolerance, where DCA does not tolerate any form of exploitation, abuse and harassment by DCA staff, volunteers, or by implementing partners. DCA is therefore committed to the prevention, detection and investigation of all forms of exploitation, abuse and harassment, in all its offices and among its implementing partners. Everyone applying for a job with DCA must be ready to comply with our Staff Policy on Prevention of Sexual Exploitation, Abuse and Harassment and our Child Safeguarding Policy.

​Position Title: Project Officer – Humanitarian Response
​Location: Rasuwa, Nuwakot or Dhading, Nepal
Reports to: DIDRM Coordinator
Application Deadline: Application will remain open until a suitable candidate is identified.
Contract Type: Fixed term
Contract Duration: Till February 2027
Closing Date: 30/09/2026

About CBM Global

CBM Global works alongside people with disabilities in low- and middle-income countries to fight poverty and exclusion and transform lives. Check out our website and LinkedIn profile to learn more. Drawing on over 100 years of experience, we work with the most marginalised in society to:

  • Break the cycle of poverty and disability
  • Treat and prevent conditions that lead to disability; and
  • Build inclusive communities where everyone can enjoy their human rights and achieve their full potential.We work in over 20 countries, investing in long-term, authentic partnerships with the Disability Movement and multiplying our impact by delivering a combination of inclusive community-based programmes, advocacy for national and global policy change and inclusion advice to other organisations. CBM Global is a worldwide federation with the following Members: CBM Australia, CBM Ireland, CBM Kenya, CBM New Zealand, CBM Switzerland, and CBM UK.

About the Role

​
CBM Global Nepal has initiated a humanitarian response in areas affected by the devastating flash floods in the Bhotekoshi River and downstream river systems. The response covers affected communities in the Rasuwa, Nuwakot, and Dhading districts and focuses on mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS), basic needs assistance, provision of assistive devices, rehabilitation services, and advocacy and technical support to ensure the inclusion of persons with disabilities in the overall humanitarian response.

The Humanitarian Response Project Officer will be responsible for coordinating humanitarian response interventions in close collaboration with partner organizations. The position provides overall oversight of project implementation, including partner support, budget management, monitoring, documentation, and reporting. S/he will serve as the focal point for project implementation with partners and stakeholders on behalf of CBM Global Nepal.

​

Key Responsibilities

​​

A. Project Implementation Oversight

​

  • ​Guide and support the implementation of humanitarian response activities in accordance with the project plans, budgets, and timelines.
  • Oversee coordination among partners to ensure coherent and effective implementation.
  • Ensure strong coordination and collaboration with project stakeholders, including Organizations of Persons with Disabilities (OPDs), local governments, cluster mechanisms, and other humanitarian stakeholders.
  • Ensure project interventions adhere to quality standards, humanitarian principles, and organizational policies.
  • Monitor activities and resource utilization to ensure efficiency, effectiveness, and value for money.
  • Manage project finances in close coordination with the finance team
  • Identify implementation challenges, risks, and bottlenecks, and propose appropriate mitigation measures.
  • Support rapid and ongoing needs assessments, identify emerging humanitarian needs and recommend timely adaptations to response activities.
    ​

B. Partner Coordination and Support

​

  • Manage partner relations and maintain close collaboration with all project partners.
  • Ensure partners understand project objectives, donor requirements, and expected results.
  • Facilitate regular coordination meetings with partners to review progress, address challenges, and ensure timely implementation.
  • Participate in technical meetings with local authorities, clusters, NGOs, and relevant institutions, and share key updates with the line manager.
  • Serve as the primary focal point for partners on behalf of CBM Global Nepal.
    ​

C. Monitoring, Documentation and Reporting

​

  • Conduct regular monitoring visits to project sites to ensure quality implementation and achievement of project objectives.
  • Track project indicators and maintain accurate project records and databases.
  • Generate evidence through systematic documentation of best practices, lessons learned, success stories, and case studies.
  • Coordinate the preparation and submission of high-quality reports in a timely manner.
  • Support partners in data collection, analysis, and reporting processes.
  • Support partners to establish and implement inclusive, accessible, and effective feedback, complaints, and response mechanisms (FCRM), ensuring meaningful participation of persons with disabilities.
    ​

F. Safeguarding

​

​Knowledge

Understands the incident management framework and their first responder role in recording, responding and reporting incidents.

Understands the survivor-centered approach and how to apply it when receiving a complaint or responding to an incident. Knows local support services available in the community or region, and how to engage them.

Skills

Able to listen and accurately document reported concerns and complaints. Able to respect the confidentiality of safeguarding allegations. Able to appropriately apply the survivor-centred approach.

Behaviours

Treats the survivor and others involved in an incident with dignity and respect.

Be assertive in implementing the initial incident response protocols by gaining the trust and cooperation of parties involved.
​

Who We’re Looking For

We are looking for a candidate who brings the following experience and qualities:

All the following requirements are Essential, unless marked with a * when they are Desirable.

Experience and Knowledge

​

  • A minimum of 3 years of experience in managing development and/or humanitarian projects in I/NGOs.
  • Experience in managing disability inclusive humanitarian response or recovery projects/ programmes preferred.*
  • Experience working simultaneously with multiple partners.
  • Experience working with Organizations of Persons with Disabilities (OPDs) preferred.*
  • Experience engaging with local government systems, humanitarian clusters, and development partners.
  • Demonstrated experience in reporting, documentation, and knowledge management.
  • Proven experience in project financial management.
    ​

Skills/Competencies/Personal Qualities

​

  • Strong knowledge of humanitarian principles and coordination mechanisms.
  • Excellent coordination and stakeholder management skills.
  • Strong planning and organizational abilities with a results-oriented approach.
  • Flexibility and adaptability to changing work demands in emergency contexts.
  • Strong teamwork and interpersonal skills.
  • Willingness to learn, adapt, and respond to dynamic environments.
  • Knowledge of disability inclusion principles.*
  • Strong communication skills in English (oral and written).
  • Alignment to CBM Global values (Our Vision, Mission and Values | CBM Global) and Safeguarding Policy (CBM-Global-Policy-Safeguarding.pdf) and Code of Conduct (CBM-Global-Code-of-Conduct.pdf)
    ​

Qualifications

​

  • Minimum Bachelor’s degree in Social Sciences, Disaster Risk Management, Development Studies, or a related field.
  • Master’s degree in a relevant discipline is preferred*.
    ​

We welcome and encourage applications from people with lived experience of disability.

​

We proactively work on achieving a diverse and inclusive work environment for people from all backgrounds and abilities.

​

Why work with Us?

​

  • A chance to be part of a global movement pursuing an inclusive world for people with disabilities.
  • A supportive, flexible, and inclusive work environment.
  • Flexible working arrangements.
  • A culture that champions Mental Health and Wellbeing.
  • Opportunities for learning, growth, and international collaboration.
  • Competitive remuneration and benefits.
    ​

Hear from our colleagues

Colleagues from Philippines Country Team say:

”Join CBM Global: We embody the culture of support, growth, and impact.”

​

Colleagues from Nigeria Country Team say:

”At CBM Global you are not just a staff but a change maker.”

Colleagues from Lao PDR Country Team say:

Colleagues from Nepal Country Team say:

Then Join Us and Be Part of the Change!

Save the Children believes every child deserves a future. In Bhutan and around the world, we give children a healthy start in life, the opportunity to learn and protection from harm. We do whatever it takes for children – every day and in times of crisis – transforming their lives and future we share. Save the Children is the leading independent organization for children. We save children’s lives; we fight for their rights; we help them fulfill their potential. The Field Operations Lead will serve as the primary focal point in the field, overseeing day-to-day response implementation, representing the response team at local coordination forums, managing communications and stakeholder engagement, and ensuring timely reporting and visibility of response activities. The position will oversee operational planning, team management, coordination with government and humanitarian actors, response monitoring, and contribute in the development of situation reports and donor updates.

The WASH Coordinator will provide technical and operational leadership in planning, implementing, monitoring, and reporting flood response WASH interventions. The position will ensure quality delivery of emergency water supply, sanitation, and hygiene promotion activities and coordinate with government authorities, humanitarian partners, and the WASH Cluster. The position will provide technical leadership to ensure quality implementation of water supply, sanitation, and hygiene promotion activities and represent the organization in relevant WASH coordination forums and clusters.

Conduct WASH needs assessments in target communities, schools, health facilities, collective centers, CFS, and other project sites.
Identify gaps and priorities related to water supply, sanitation, hygiene practices, and infrastructure.
Collect, analyze, and document assessment findings to support program planning and decision-making.
Develop detail implementation plan and recommendations for appropriate WASH interventions based on assessment results.
Ensure community participation, including women, men, girls, boys, and marginalized groups, during such assessments in coordination with the stakeholders and PDQI department
Provide technical assistance for the repair, rehabilitation, and maintenance of small-scale water supply systems and conduct technical inspections and assessments of water schemes.
Ensure water systems meet quality and safety standards.
Build the capacity of community members and user committees on operation and maintenance of water systems.
Monitor functionality and sustainability of rehabilitated water supply facilities.
Provide technical guidance on the design and construction of gender-friendly, accessible, and inclusive sanitation facilities and integration of disability-friendly features in sanitation facilities.
Ensure installation of appropriate handwashing stations with soap and water near sanitation facilities.
Monitor construction quality and compliance with WASH standards.
Coordinate with contractors, local authorities, and community stakeholders during implementation.
Coordinate, mentor, support on capacity development and project implementation to WASH staffs working for partner organization.
Develop and implement hygiene promotion and behavior change activities.
Conduct awareness and sensitization sessions on safe water handling, sanitation, menstrual hygiene management, handwashing, and disease prevention.
Develop or adapt SBC materials for WASH promotion activities in consultation with the PDQI department
Train community volunteers, teachers, health workers, and local stakeholders on WASH and hygiene practices.
Monitor the effectiveness of hygiene promotion interventions and recommend improvements.
Develop activity plans and monitor implementation progress against project targets.
Maintain accurate records of assessments, trainings, infrastructure activities, and community interventions.
Represent SCI in WASH Cluster meetings, technical working groups, and coordination forums.
Share project updates, challenges, and achievements with relevant stakeholders.
Ensure alignment of project activities with national WASH standards, policies, and cluster guidelines.
Report incidents, risks, and access constraints promptly.
Ensure data and the information from the field are regularly updated to the relevant teams and departments in the Country Office.

Swisscontact, established in 1959 in Switzerland, is a leading partner organisation for the implementation of international development projects. The organisation promotes inclusive economic, social, and ecological development to make an effective contribution towards sustainable and widespread prosperity in developing and emerging economies. It strengthens the competencies of people, improving their employability, increases the competitiveness of enterprises, growing their business, and fosters social and economic systems, promoting inclusive development.

Swisscontact, registered as an International Non-Governmental Organisation in Nepal, has been operating in Nepal since 1991. Currently, Swisscontact in Nepal has six development programmes across all seven provinces.

The Municipal Revenue Enhancement Project (MunRev) is a bilateral initiative of the Governments of Nepal and Switzerland, implemented by the Ministry of Land Management, Cooperatives, Federal Affairs and General Administration (MoLMCFAGA) and selected 12 partner municipalities of Koshi and Bagmati Provinces, with technical assistance from Swisscontact in Nepal. MunRev supports local governments to strengthen own-source revenue and tax compliance, improve inclusive and transparent public service delivery, and foster cross-government learning for better-informed fiscal policy, with gender equality and social inclusion (GESI) mainstreamed throughout. Through these efforts, the project aims to enhance the fiscal capacity of local governments and improve services for all citizens, including women and disadvantaged groups.

Swisscontact in Nepal invites applications from the committed and experienced Nepali citizens for the following positions.

title.rendered: Social Mobilizer, Assistant Logistics Officer, Support Staff (Office Assistant), MEAL Officer, Admin and Finance Officer, Program Officer, Sub-Overseer, Program Coordinator, Civil Engineer, Volunteer/ Enumerator

content.rendered:
Bagmati Welfare Society Nepal (BWSN) is a women-led and youth-led feminist organization established in 1995 in Sarlahi, Nepal. For thirty two years BWSN has worked in the districts where public systems arrived last, and currently works across 201 local levels in Madhesh, Koshi, Lumbini, Karnali and Bagmati Provinces. Its work is organized around three pillars — People, Planet and Power: human wellbeing and social development, climate resilience and biodiversity, and inclusive governance and civic engagement.

The Response

On 26 August 2026, an ice-rock collapse near the Nepal–China border blocked the Lhende Khola. The lake that formed behind the blockage breached and sent a flash flood down the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli rivers. There was no rainfall and no warning, and the Syabrubesi gauging station was destroyed in the flood. The Government of Nepal has declared 15 local levels across five districts disaster crisis-hit for three months under Section 32(1) of the Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Act, 2074.

BWSN deployed a response team within hours and coordinated the response from Nuwakot. BWSN is working alongside rural municipalities, municipalities and district authorities on needs assessment, beneficiary identification, delivery and follow-up.

BWSN invites applications from qualified and committed Nepali candidates for the following positions.

Duty Stations: Nuwakot, Dhading and Rasuwa Districts, Bagmati Province

Positions Available

  • Program Coordinator
  • Admin and Finance Officer
  • Civil Engineer
  • Sub-Overseer
  • Program Officer
  • Social Mobilizer
  • Psychosocial Support (PSS) Coordinator
  • Psychosocial Counsellor
  • Child Protection and Safeguarding Officer
  • MEAL Officer
  • Assistant Logistics Officer
  • Support Staff (Office Assistant)
  • Volunteer/ Enumerator

Position Descriptions

1. Program Coordinator

Key responsibilities

  • Lead rapid and follow-up WASH assessments in flood-affected wards and displacement sites, working through ward offices and municipal WASH focal points rather than conducting parallel assessments.
  • Plan and oversee emergency water supply, sanitation and hygiene interventions, including restoration of damaged water points, water treatment and safe storage, emergency latrines and solid waste management.
  • Represent BWSN in the district WASH Cluster and in municipal coordination meetings in Bidur, Tarkeshwor and Rasuwa, and ensure BWSN’s planned coverage is registered with local government to avoid duplication and gaps.
  • Agree WASH beneficiary lists with rural municipality and municipality officials under the one-door system, and ensure BWSN activity is recorded in local government reporting.
  • Ensure interventions meet Sphere and national WASH standards, and monitor water quality and public health risk, including acute watery diarrhoea and other outbreak risk in displacement sites.
  • Supervise WASH-related work of Social Mobilizers, volunteers, contractors and suppliers, and verify quality of delivered works and materials.
  • Prepare WASH technical specifications, work plans, budgets, activity reports and inputs to donor reporting.

Minimum qualification and experience

  • Bachelor’s degree in water supply and Sanitation, Public Health, Environmental Science or a related discipline.
  • Minimum 3–5 years of relevant professional experience, of which at least one year in emergency or humanitarian WASH programming.
  • Demonstrated experience coordinating with local government and cluster mechanisms in Nepal.
  • Working knowledge of Sphere standards and national WASH design norms.

2. Admin and Finance Officer

Key responsibilities

  • Manage day-to-day financial transactions of the response, including field advances, cash handling in locations without banking access and timely settlement of advances.
  • Maintain complete accounting records, vouchers, ledgers and supporting documentation for every distribution, procurement and payment.
  • Run procurement in line with BWSN policy and donor requirements, including quotation, comparison, approval and contracting records under emergency provisions.
  • Prepare and monitor budgets, track expenditure against the approved budget, and flag variances and funding gaps to the Program Coordinator early.
  • Maintain the documentation that demonstrates relief delivered through local government has been properly accounted for, including handover and receipt records.
  • Handle personnel administration for the field team, including attendance, leave records, contracts, insurance and orientation documentation.
  • Maintain office and asset records, agreements, and the response filing system in both hard and soft copy.
  • Prepare periodic financial reports and inputs to donor financial reporting, internal review and external audit.

Minimum qualification and experience

  • Bachelor’s degree in management, Accounting, Finance or a related discipline.
  • Minimum 3 years of relevant experience, preferably with NGOs, INGOs or donor-funded projects.
  • Proficiency in accounting software and strong Microsoft Excel skills.
  • High standard of integrity, confidentiality and attention to detail.

3. Civil Engineer

Key responsibilities

  • Support emergency flood response and recovery activities in affected communities and field locations.
  • Conduct rapid assessment of damaged houses, roads, bridges, water systems, and other infrastructure.
  • Collect, verify, and document technical and damage assessment data from affected areas.
  • Support the preparation of site assessments, measurements, BOQs, cost estimates, and technical reports.
  • Provide technical support for repair, rehabilitation, and reconstruction of community infrastructure.
  • Monitor construction and repair works to ensure compliance with approved designs, specifications, quality, and safety standards.
  • Coordinate with contractors, local authorities, community representatives, and field teams during implementation.
  • Support the identification of priority infrastructure needs and emergency rehabilitation requirements.
  • Maintain accurate records of site visits, measurements, photographs, progress, materials, and technical documentation.
  • Provide regular updates on progress, challenges, quality issues, and technical gaps to the Program Coordinator.
  • Perform other technical and emergency response duties assigned by the organization.

Minimum qualification and experience

  • Bachelors in Civil Engineering or equivalent; registration with the Nepal Engineering Council is an advantage.
  • Minimum 2–3 years of relevant site supervision experience; experience in rural water supply, sanitation or post-disaster reconstruction is preferred.
  • Ability to prepare estimates and use relevant design and drawing software.
  • Willingness to work at field sites daily in difficult terrain.

4. Sub-Overseer

Key responsibilities

  • Carry out technical assessment of damaged water supply systems, water points, sanitation facilities and small community infrastructure in the affected wards.
  • Prepare drawings, estimates, bills of quantity and technical specifications for repair and emergency construction works.
  • Supervise construction and repair works on site, including water source protection, pipeline and tap stand repair, emergency latrines and drainage.
  • Verify quality and quantity of materials delivered and works completed and certify measurement books and running bills before payment.
  • Coordinate technical planning with the municipal or rural municipality technical section and ward offices so that works align with local government plans.
  • Ensure works are safe, accessible and usable by women, children, older persons and persons with disabilities.
  • Maintain site records, progress reports, photographs and completion documentation.

Minimum qualification and experience

  • Diploma in Civil Engineering (Overseer level) or equivalent; registration with the Nepal Engineering Council is an advantage.
  • Minimum 2–3 years of relevant site supervision experience; experience in rural water supply, sanitation or post-disaster reconstruction is preferred.
  • Ability to prepare estimates and use relevant design and drawing software.
  • Willingness to work at field sites daily in difficult terrain.

5. Program Officer

Key responsibilities

  • Support day-to-day implementation of response activities and translate the workplan into weekly and daily field plans.
  • Organise assessments, beneficiary identification, verification and distribution activities in coordination with ward offices and local government.
  • Supervise and support Social Mobilizers in the field, and ensure activities reach the households identified as most at risk.
  • Facilitate coordination meetings at ward and municipal level and maintain working relationships with local officials, community leaders and other agencies.
  • Ensure hygiene promotion, protection messaging and referral information reach affected communities through the field team.
  • Compile field data, activity records and photographs, and prepare activity reports for the Program Coordinator.
  • Support accountability to affected populations, including communication of entitlements, selection criteria and how to raise a complaint.
  • Deputise for the Program Coordinator on specific tasks as delegated.

Minimum qualification and experience

  • Bachelor’s degree in Social Work, Development Studies, Public Health, Sociology or a related discipline.
  • Minimum 3 years of relevant field implementation experience; emergency response experience is preferred.
  • Good written and spoken English and strong report-writing ability.
  • Experience supervising field-level staff or volunteers.

6. Social Mobilizer

Key responsibilities

  • Work at ward level with ward chairpersons, ward secretaries, tole committees and local groups to support needs assessment and household identification.
  • Support verification of beneficiary lists prepared by the local government, and raise omissions, duplications and exclusion of vulnerable households with the ward office and the BWSN team.
  • Facilitate community meetings and awareness sessions on hygiene, safe water, sanitation, available services and how to raise a complaint.
  • Ensure women, children, older persons, persons with disabilities, single women, pregnant and lactating women, and socially excluded households are reached and able to participate.
  • Identify and refer individuals needing psychosocial, protection, health or specialised support to the relevant service provider, and follow up on referrals made.
  • Collect community feedback and complaints and pass them to the MEAL Officer for logging and follow-up.
  • Support distribution days, including crowd and queue management, verification at the point of distribution, and follow-up with households unable to attend.

Minimum qualification and experience

  • Minimum +2 or intermediate level; a bachelor’s degree in social work, Sociology, Development Studies, Education or a related field is an advantage.
  • Minimum 1–2 years of community mobilisation experience; experience in emergency response is preferred.
  • Fluency in Nepali; knowledge of Tamang or other local languages spoken in Nuwakot and Rasuwa is a strong advantage.
  • Candidates from the affected wards and districts are particularly encouraged to apply.

7. Psychosocial Support (PSS) Coordinator

Key responsibilities

  • Lead the design and implementation of community-based mental health and psychosocial support activities across the response area.
  • Coordinate rapid identification of psychosocial needs among children, adolescents, adults, older persons and bereaved households, including those who lost family members or homes in the flood.
  • Establish safe, private and confidential spaces for individual and group support in displacement sites and host communities, in agreement with the local government and site management.
  • Supervise and provide technical support and regular case discussion to Psychosocial Counsellors and community-based psychosocial workers.
  • Map and maintain referral pathways to district hospitals, mental health services, the One-Stop Crisis Management Centre, police and protection actors, and agree these pathways with the district authorities.
  • Represent BWSN in protection and MHPSS coordination at district level and with the local government.
  • Ensure PSS activity follows ethical, confidential, person-centred, survivor-centred and Do No Harm principles, and that no case information is shared outside agreed referral protocols.
  • Organise staff care and peer support for BWSN staff and volunteers working in response, and monitor and report on PSS activity.

Minimum qualification and experience

  • Bachelor’s or master’s degree in psychology, Counselling Psychology, Clinical Psychology, Social Work or a related discipline.
  • Minimum 3–5 years of relevant experience, preferably including humanitarian or emergency settings.
  • Training and practical experience in Psychological First Aid, trauma-informed approaches and community-based MHPSS.
  • Demonstrated supervision experience.

8. Psychosocial Counsellor

Key responsibilities

  • Provide individual and group psychosocial support and basic counselling to flood-affected individuals in displacement sites and host communities.
  • Provide Psychological First Aid to people in acute distress, including those bereaved, displaced or separated from family members.
  • Identify people requiring specialized mental health, medical or protection support and make safe, consented referrals through the agreed pathways.
  • Facilitate awareness sessions on stress, grief, coping and available services, adapted for children, adolescents and adults.
  • Support child-friendly and community-based psychosocial activities in coordination with the Child Protection and Safeguarding Officer.
  • Maintain confidential, accurate and minimal case documentation in line with BWSN data protection requirements.
  • Report caseload patterns and emerging concerns to the PSS Coordinator, without disclosing identifying information beyond agreed protocols.

Minimum qualification and experience

  • Bachelor’s degree in psychology, Counselling, Social Work or a related field.
  • Minimum 2 years of counselling or psychosocial support experience is preferred.
  • Training in Psychological First Aid, trauma-informed care or humanitarian MHPSS is an advantage.
  • Ability to work sensitively with people who have experienced sudden loss and displacement.

9. Child Protection and Safeguarding Officer

Key responsibilities

  • Lead child protection and safeguarding work across the response, including risk identification in displacement sites, distribution points and host communities.
  • Identify protection risks affecting children, including family separation, unaccompanied and separated children, child labour, trafficking risk, early marriage, violence, exploitation and neglect.
  • Work with the local government, Nepal Police, the Municipal Child Rights Committee and protection actors on identification, family tracing and case referral for unaccompanied and separated children.
  • Establish and maintain safe referral pathways for children and families requiring specialized services and agree with district authorities.
  • Review distribution and activity plans for child safety and accessibility and advise on changes where activities create risk.
  • Deliver safeguarding, PSEA and Code of Conduct orientation to BWSN staff, volunteers, contractors and, where relevant, community members and local government partners.
  • Ensure safeguarding and PSEA reporting channels are known, accessible and functioning, and that reports are handled confidentially and escalated according to BWSN policy.

Minimum qualification and experience

  • Bachelor’s degree in social work, Psychology, Sociology, Child Development, Law, Development Studies or a related discipline.
  • Minimum 3 years of experience in child protection, safeguarding or protection programming, including in emergency settings.
  • Working knowledge of Nepal’s child protection framework, PSEA standards and referral mechanisms.
  • Experience delivering safeguarding orientation and handling sensitive reports.

10. MEAL Officer

Key responsibilities

  • Set up and run the MEAL system for the response, including assessment tools, beneficiary tracking, distribution and post-distribution monitoring formats and reporting templates.
  • Reconcile BWSN beneficiary records with local government lists prepared under the one-door system, and document how selection decisions were made and by whom.
  • Carry out field monitoring and post-distribution monitoring in Nuwakot and Rasuwa, including verification visits to households recorded as assisted.
  • Establish and manage the Community Feedback and Complaints Response Mechanism, ensure complaints are logged, routed and closed, and report trends to the response team.
  • Prepare situation reports, dashboards and figures for donor and government reporting, using NDRRMA and district figures as the reference source for caseload data.
  • Document lessons learned, adaptations and good practice through the response, including what worked and did not work in coordination with local government.
  • Ensure all data is collected, stored and shared ethically and confidentially, with particular care for protection and psychosocial case data.

Minimum qualification and experience

  • Bachelor’s degree in Statistics, Development Studies, Social Sciences, Public Health, Economics or a related discipline.
  • Minimum 3 years of relevant MEAL or M&E experience, preferably including humanitarian or emergency response.
  • Working proficiency in Kobo Toolbox or ODK and in Microsoft Excel, including data cleaning and basic analysis.
  • Ability to produce clear written analysis in English.

11. Assistant Logistics Officer

Key responsibilities

  • Manage receipt, storage, stock recording and dispatch of relief materials, including items released from the BWSN warehouse and procured locally.
  • Maintain bin cards, stock ledgers, goods received notes, waybills and distribution handover records, and reconcile physical stock with records regularly.
  • Arrange transport to field sites, including in areas where access is by alternative routes, on foot or by porter, and plan loading and offloading.
  • Support procurement by collecting quotations, checking specifications and verifying deliveries against purchase orders.
  • Arrange logistics for distribution days, including site setup, storage at the point of distribution and return of unissued stock.
  • Support fleet, fuel and travel arrangements for the field team and maintain related records.
  • Report stock levels, losses, damage and pipeline gaps to the Admin and Finance Officer and Program Coordinator.

Minimum qualification and experience

  • Minimum +2 or intermediate level; a bachelor’s degree in management or a related field is an advantage.
  • Minimum 2 years of experience in logistics, storekeeping or supply chain, preferably with NGOs or in humanitarian operations.
  • Practical experience of warehouse and stock documentation.
  • A valid two-wheeler driving license is an advantage.

12. Volunteers/Enumerators

Key responsibilities

  • Support emergency flood response activities in affected communities and field locations.
  • Assist in the collection, verification, and recording of beneficiary and household data.
  • Conduct field-level data collection and needs assessments from flood-affected communities.
  • Enter and maintain accurate data in Excel, databases, or other reporting systems.
  • Support the preparation and updating of beneficiary lists, distribution records, and field reports.
  • Assist the team in identifying and documenting priority needs, damages, and gaps during the emergency response.
  • Support the distribution of relief materials and maintain related records.
  • Collect and organize information, photos, forms, and other field documentation as required.
  • Coordinate with field teams and community representatives to ensure accurate and timely information collection.
  • Perform other emergency response and administrative tasks assigned by the Program Coordinator or Admin and Finance Officer.

Minimum qualification and experience

  • Minimum +2 or intermediate level.
  • Experiences in data collection, data entry, volunteer, preferably with NGOs or in humanitarian operations.
  • A valid two-wheeler driving license is an advantage.
  • Strong and good communication skills.

General Requirements for All Positions

The following apply to every position advertised above and are not repeated in the individual descriptions.

  • Commitment to humanitarian principles, accountability to affected populations, safeguarding and inclusion.
  • Ability to work in a coordination-led response in which BWSN supports and works through local government rather than delivering independently.
  • Fluency in written and spoken Nepali. Good written and spoken English is required for the Program Coordinator, Program Officer, MEAL, Admin and Finance, PSS Coordinator and Child Protection positions.
  • Ability to work in high-pressure conditions with long hours, shifting priorities and incomplete information.
  • Good communication, teamwork and coordination skills, and the ability to work respectfully with local government, communities, other agencies and security forces.
  • Commitment to gender equality, disability inclusion and the protection of vulnerable groups.
  • Nepali citizenship and a valid citizenship certificate.

Safeguarding and Code of Conduct

BWSN maintains a zero-tolerance approach to sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment, child abuse, discrimination, fraud and other misconduct. All selected candidates are required to comply with BWSN’s Safeguarding Policy, Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA) Policy, Child Protection Policy, Code of Conduct and related organizational policies, and to sign them on appointment.

Appointment is subject to satisfactory reference checks, including checks with previous humanitarian employers on conduct, background checks, and verification of academic and professional qualifications. BWSN will seek references on safeguarding conduct and will not proceed with an appointment where these cannot be obtained.

Who We Encourage to Apply

BWSN particularly encourages applications from women, young professionals, persons with disabilities, and candidates from Dalit, Janajati, Madhesi and other socially excluded communities. Candidates from Nuwakot, Dhading and Rasuwa and from the affected communities are strongly encouraged to apply and will be prioritised where qualifications and experience are comparable, in recognition of local language, local knowledge and the ability to work in the response area immediately.

How to Apply

Interested and qualified candidates should submit the following:

  • An updated CV.
  • A cover letter clearly stating the position applied for and the preferred duty station.
  • Contact details of two professional referees.
  • Please mention your expected salary in cover letter.

Email: hr@bwsn.org.np

Email subject line: Application – [Position Title] – Bhotekoshi Flood Response 2026

Application deadline: 7 September 2026, 17:00 (Nepal Standard Time)

Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis, and positions may be filled before the deadline. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. BWSN may conduct written tests, practical assessments and interviews, and may amend or cancel this announcement. Canvassing disqualifies an application. This recruitment is subject to funding availability.
